section: 45. Conclusion
text:
45. Conclusion
Gravity does not need to begin with a force between already-complete masses.
A weak-field planetary system first presents a recurrent shared relation.
Kepler I gives its closure geometry:
\[r(\theta)=\frac{p}{1+e\cos\theta}.\]
Kepler II gives its areal recurrence:
\[J_K=r^2\dot\theta=\text{constant}.\]
Together they require purely radial relative coordinate acceleration:
\[\frac{d^2\mathbf r}{dt^2}=-\mu_G\frac{\mathbf r}{r^3},\]
with

\[\mu_G=\frac{J_K^2}{p}.\]
No gravitational force has been assumed.
Kepler III then gives
\[\mu_G=\frac{4\pi^2a^3}{T^2}.\]
and shows that one coefficient organizes an entire family of bound closures.
The test-body mass remains absent.
This is exactly what should be expected after Addendum 37.
A freely falling boundary need not possess local proper acceleration:
\[a^{\mathrm{prop}}=0.\]
Its relative position can nevertheless change relative to a larger gravitational reference.
The Keplerian inverse-square law is the weak-field coordinate read of that shared free-fall organization.
Only afterward does Newtonian mechanical calibration introduce force.
In the test-body limit,
\[\mu_G=GM\]
and
\[\mathbf F_N=-\frac{GMm}{r^3}\mathbf r.\]
For two comparable bodies,
\[\mu_G=G(m_1+m_2),\]
making the shared-boundary ownership explicit.
The gravitational parameter measured by closure therefore comes before its decomposition into gravitational coupling and source mass.
The orbital free-fall relation comes before the force used to represent it.
And the dynamic swept area of Keplerian recurrence points toward the next geometric inversion: under spherical projection, the inverse-square law becomes an inverse-area relation.

That problem belongs to Addendum 41.
The resulting hierarchy is
peer boundaries → shared gravitational closure → elliptical geometry → areal recurrence → inverse-square free fa
Thus:

Keplerian closure occurs before gravitational force.

title: Addendum 41 — Gravitational Area Occurs Before Areal Radius
section: Abstract
text:
Abstract
Newtonian gravity is conventionally written in terms of radial distance:
\[g_G=\frac{\mu_G}{r^2},\]
or, after source calibration,
\[g_G=\frac{GM}{r^2}.\]
The appearance of r is so familiar that radial distance is easily treated as the primitive geometric variable from which the enclosing spherical area
\[A=4\pi r^2.\]
is subsequently constructed.
Recursively Realized Distinguishability (R²D) permits the opposite explanatory order.
Addendum 40 derived the inverse-square relative free-fall relation directly from Keplerian closure:
\[\frac{d^2\mathbf r}{dt^2}=-\mu_G\frac{\mathbf r}{r^3},\]
with
\[\mu_G=\frac{4\pi^2a^3}{T^2}.\]
shared by a family of orbital closures belonging to the same gravitational relation.
That result does not yet establish a primitive spherical radius. It establishes a radial dependence within an empirically readable orbital closure.
The present addendum asks what geometric quantity that radial dependence represents when the enclosing gravitational relation is additionally spherically symmetric.
Let

\[B_G\]
denote the shared gravitational boundary.
The formal R²D boundary is not itself a geometric sphere. When it acquires a spherically symmetric spatial projection, let the corresponding enclosing symmetry surface possess physical area
\[A_G.\]
Only afterward define the associated areal radius
\[r_A\equiv\sqrt{\frac{A_G}{4\pi}}.\]
Thus
\[A_G\longrightarrow r_A.\]
The Keplerian inverse-square law then becomes
\[g_G=\frac{\mu_G}{r_A^2}=\frac{4\pi\mu_G}{A_G}.\]
Therefore,
\[g_GA_G=4\pi\mu_G.\]
The familiar inverse-square radial law is the spherical coordinate representation of a prior inverse-area gravitational relation.
The distinction becomes more important in strong gravity.
In a spherically symmetric spacetime, the areal radius remains defined exactly by
\[A_G=4\pi r_A^2.\]
Curvature does not invalidate that definition.
Instead, curvature changes the relation between areal radius and proper radial distance.
Let
\[\ell_r\]
denote proper radial distance. In general,
\[d\ell_r\ne dr_A.\]

For Schwarzschild geometry,
\[d\ell_r=\frac{dr_A}{\sqrt{1-\frac{2GM}{c^2r_A}}}.\]
on a Schwarzschild-time spatial slice outside the horizon.
Thus three quantities that coincide approximately in weak-field Euclidean intuition become distinct:
\[r_K\ne r_A\ne\ell_r\]
in their general physical roles.
The Keplerian coordinate rK belongs to orbital peer separation.
The areal radius rA parameterizes enclosing spherical area.
The proper radial distance \(\ell_r\) is reconstructed from the local radial metric.
The complete R²D ordering is therefore

gravitational boundary → enclosing area → areal radius → proper radial ruler.

This provides the geometric coordinate needed for the next step.
Define the area-first compactness
\[\chi_G\equiv\frac{2\mu_G}{c^2r_A}.\]
Since
\[r_A=\sqrt{\frac{A_G}{4\pi}},\]
we may write
\[\chi_G=\frac{2\mu_G}{c^2}\sqrt{\frac{4\pi}{A_G}}.\]
The Schwarzschild horizon condition is not imposed here.
The present result is prior:

gravitational area occurs before areal radius.

7. Why “Areal Radius” Matters
The subscript A should remain explicit.
The quantity
\[r_A\]

does not initially mean:

• proper radial distance; • affine distance; • radar distance; • coordinate distance in an arbitrary chart; • or Euclidean ruler length from an origin.

It means exactly:
\[r_A=\sqrt{\frac{\text{area of the symmetry sphere}}{4\pi}}.\]
That definition remains meaningful even when radial proper distance is strongly curved.

In the weak-field spherical regime, the orbital radial coordinate can be identified with the spherical areal coordinate to the relevant approximation:
\[r_K\longrightarrow r_A.\]
Then Addendum 40’s acceleration law becomes
\[g_G=\frac{\mu_G}{r_A^2}.\]
This is now a spherical enclosing-space representation of the Kepler-derived free-fall relation.

9. Rewrite Gravity in Area Form
Since
\[r_A^2=\frac{A_G}{4\pi},\]
we have
\[g_G=\frac{\mu_G}{A_G/(4\pi)}.\]
Therefore,
\[g_G=\frac{4\pi\mu_G}{A_G}.\]

Equivalently,
\[g_GA_G=4\pi\mu_G.\]
This is the area-first gravitational relation.

text:
10. The Inverse-Square Law Is an Inverse-Area Law
The radial form is
\[g_G=\frac{\mu_G}{r_A^2}.\]
The enclosing-area form is
\[g_G=\frac{4\pi\mu_G}{A_G}.\]
They are mathematically equivalent.
But their logical positions differ.
The area form refers directly to the enclosing spherical relation.
The radial form appears only after the enclosing area has been encoded by one scalar parameter.
Thus:

inverse area \(\longrightarrow\) inverse-square areal radius.

The factor
\[r_A^{-2}\]
arises because spherical area satisfies
\[A_G=4\pi r_A^2.\]
Thus the exponent two is a property of the spherical geometric projection.
It does not by itself identify the underlying physical coupling.

Gravity and other inverse-area phenomena can share this exponent while possessing different local coupling structures.
Therefore:

common \(1/r^2\) \(\not\Rightarrow\) common physical ontology.

12. Kepler Shows That Area Is Not an Arbitrary Rewrite
One could object that replacing
\[r^2\]
with
\[A_G/(4\pi)\]
is merely algebra.
Kepler makes the area interpretation physically motivated.
The orbital closure already supplies a dynamically readable area:
\[\frac{dA_K}{dt}=\text{constant}.\]
Area appears in the empirical gravitational closure before Newtonian force language is introduced.
The enclosing spherical area
\[A_G\]
is not the same area.
But gravity is already organized through an areal coordinate class before the radial force interpretation is imposed.

The Keplerian swept area is
\[A_K.\]
It is planar and dynamic.

The enclosing gravitational area is
\[A_G.\]
It is the area of a spherical symmetry surface.
Thus:
\[A_K\ne A_G.\]
The legitimate sequence is structural:

areal orbital recurrence \(\longrightarrow 1/r^2\longrightarrow 1/A_G\).

No literal surface transforms into another.

text:
14. The Flux Form Makes the Enclosing Structure Explicit
For a spherically symmetric inward free-fall field,
\[\mathbf g_G=-\frac{\mu_G}{r_A^2}\hat{\mathbf r}.\]
The flux through a symmetry sphere is
\[\Phi_G=\oint\mathbf g_G\cdot d\mathbf A.\]
Because the magnitude is constant over the sphere,
\[\Phi_G=-g_GA_G.\]
Using
\[g_GA_G=4\pi\mu_G,\]
we obtain
\[\Phi_G=-4\pi\mu_G.\]
The orbital calibration supplied by Kepler has become an enclosing flux calibration.

Therefore,
\[\Phi_G=-4\pi GM.\]
This is the familiar Newtonian gravitational Gauss relation.

Keplerian closure → μG → enclosing area → gravitational flux → GM calibration.

to establish the logical priority of area over areal radius.

\[\ell_r\]
denote proper spatial distance measured along a specified radial spatial path.
In a metric representation,
\[d\ell_r=\sqrt{g_{r_Ar_A}}\,dr_A.\]
for the relevant radial spatial slice.

\[\ell_r\]
depends on both the areal coordinate and the local radial geometry.
It is farther downstream.

text:
23. The Weak-Field Limit Hides These Distinctions
In weak approximately Euclidean geometry,
\[g_{r_Ar_A}\simeq1.\]
Therefore,
\[d\ell_r\simeq dr_A.\]
Likewise, the Keplerian radial coordinate maps naturally onto the spherical areal coordinate:
\[r_K\simeq r_A.\]
Hence,
\[r_K\simeq r_A\simeq\ell_r\]
in the weak-field regime.
That is why one symbol r works so well in Newtonian mechanics.

text:
24. Strong Gravity Separates the Coordinates
In a strongly curved gravitational geometry,
\[g_{r_Ar_A}\ne1.\]
in general.
Then
\[d\ell_r\ne dr_A.\]
The areal coordinate and the local proper radial ruler are no longer interchangeable.
This is the geometric distinction that the weak-field approximation hides.

text:
25. The Area–Areal-Radius Relation Does Not Fail in Strong Gravity
This point is critical.
For a spherically symmetric geometry,
\[A_G=4\pi r_A^2\]
is the defining relation of areal radius.
Strong gravity does not invalidate it.
Curvature instead changes the relation between
\[r_A\]
and other distance measures.
Thus the correct strong-gravity statement is not
\[A_G\ne4\pi r_A^2.\]
It is
\[r_A\ne\ell_r\]
as physical coordinates in general.

26. Schwarzschild Geometry Makes the Distinction Explicit
In Schwarzschild coordinates, write the exterior line element as
\[ds^2=-\left(1-\frac{2GM}{c^2r_A}\right)c^2dt^2+\left(1-\frac{2GM}{c^2r_A}\right)^{-1}dr_A^2+r_A^2d\Omega^2.\]
The angular sector gives
\[A_G=4\pi r_A^2.\]
Exactly.
The coordinate rA is therefore the Schwarzschild areal radius.

27. Schwarzschild rA Is Not Proper Radial Distance
On a Schwarzschild-time spatial slice in the exterior region,
\[ds^2_{\mathrm{radial}}=\left(1-\frac{2GM}{c^2r_A}\right)^{-1}dr_A^2.\]
Therefore,
\[d\ell_r=\frac{dr_A}{\sqrt{1-\frac{2GM}{c^2r_A}}}.\]
Thus
\[d\ell_r>dr_A\]
outside the horizon for finite positive GM /rA .
The areal radius and proper radial distance are physically distinct.

Differentiate

\[A_G=4\pi r_A^2.\]

\[dr_A=\frac{dA_G}{8\pi r_A}.\]

The ruler does not ontologically precede the area it parameterizes.

30. Equal Areal Distinguishability Does Not Mean Equal Radial Distinguishability
Suppose two neighboring enclosing states differ by the same areal interval
\[\delta A_G.\]
Then the corresponding areal-radius interval is
\[\delta r_A\simeq\frac{\delta A_G}{8\pi r_A}.\]
As rA increases,
\[\delta r_A\]
for the same areal distinction becomes smaller.
Therefore:

fixed areal distinction \(\not\Rightarrow\) fixed radial distinction.

This will become important when gravitational multiplicity and horizon-state spacing are considered later.

A later gravitational boundary may appear to possess ever-finer radial intervals.

The more prior question is:

does the enclosing area distinction remain readable?

Only after the areal distinction has been specified should its radial coordinate interval be calculated.
This corrects the temptation to interpret vanishing radial spacing as a primitive gravitational limit.

areal distinguishability \(\longrightarrow\) radial distinguishability.

Established in Addendum 40
Keplerian closure gives

\[\frac{d^2\mathbf r}{dt^2}=-\mu_G\frac{\mathbf r}{r^3},\]
with
\[\mu_G=\frac{4\pi^2a^3}{T^2}.\]
New Physical Mapping Assumption
The enclosing gravitational projection is taken to be spherically symmetric.
Geometric Definition
The spherical symmetry surface has area
\[A_G,\]
and the areal radius is defined by
\[r_A=\sqrt{\frac{A_G}{4\pi}}.\]
Derived Area Law
\[g_G=\frac{4\pi\mu_G}{A_G}.\]
Derived Flux Relation
\[\oint\mathbf g_G\cdot d\mathbf A=-4\pi\mu_G.\]
Conventional Source Calibration
In the dominant-source Newtonian limit,
\[\mu_G=GM.\]
Strong-Gravity Geometric Clarification
Areal radius and proper radial distance are distinct:
\[d\ell_r=\sqrt{g_{r_Ar_A}}\,dr_A.\]
Not Derived Here
This addendum does not derive:

• spherical symmetry from primitive R²D counting;



• the numerical value or recursive origin of G; • the Schwarzschild lapse; • the Schwarzschild horizon condition; • the radial metric coefficient; • the horizon multiplicity; • the Planck-area calibration; • gravitational entropy.

Those belong downstream.

\[A_G,\]

and
\[\chi_G=\frac{2\mu_G}{c^2r_A}.\]

How does increasing gravitational compactness modify the local clock-ruler reference relation while preserving the enclosing areal coordinate?

That is the point at which the Schwarzschild lapse should enter.
Not earlier.

text:
47. Conclusion
Addendum 40 showed that Keplerian closure occurs before gravitational force.
Elliptical closure plus constant areal recurrence gives
\[\frac{d^2\mathbf r}{dt^2}=-\mu_G\frac{\mathbf r}{r^3}.\]
The coefficient
\[\mu_G=\frac{4\pi^2a^3}{T^2}.\]
belongs to the shared gravitational relation before it is decomposed into
\[GM.\]
The present addendum asks what the radial denominator means geometrically.
Under spherical projection, introduce the enclosing gravitational area
\[A_G.\]

Only afterward define
\[r_A=\sqrt{\frac{A_G}{4\pi}}.\]
Then the Keplerian law becomes
\[g_G=\frac{4\pi\mu_G}{A_G}.\]
The inverse-square radial law is therefore the scalar-radius representation of an inverse-area relation.
Its enclosing flux is
\[\oint\mathbf g_G\cdot d\mathbf A=-4\pi\mu_G.\]
After
\[\mu_G=GM,\]
this becomes the Newtonian gravitational Gauss relation.
But the most important consequence appears in strong gravity.
The defining relation
\[A_G=4\pi r_A^2\]
does not fail.
It defines areal radius.
What fails is the weak-field identification of areal radius with proper radial distance.
In general,
\[d\ell_r\ne dr_A.\]
For Schwarzschild geometry,
\[d\ell_r=\frac{dr_A}{\sqrt{1-\frac{2GM}{c^2r_A}}}.\]
Thus curved gravitational geometry does not require a primitive radius to bend.

The enclosing area remains the prior spherical read.
The areal radius parameterizes that area.
The local metric then determines how physical radial rulers represent change in that coordinate.
This also makes gravitational distinguishability area first.
From
\[dA_G=8\pi r_A\,dr_A,\]
we obtain
\[dr_A=\frac{dA_G}{8\pi r_A}.\]
The same areal distinction can therefore project onto different radial intervals depending on the enclosing geometry.
A shrinking radial interval is not itself the primitive loss of distinguishability.
One must first ask whether the areal distinction survives.
Finally, define
\[\chi_G=\frac{2\mu_G}{c^2r_A}=\frac{2\mu_G}{c^2}\sqrt{\frac{4\pi}{A_G}}.\]
This is the area-first compactness inherited by the Schwarzschild problem.
The horizon condition has not yet been imposed.
That belongs to the next addendum.
The resulting hierarchy is
shared gravitational boundary → enclosing area → areal radius → compactness → proper clock-ruler geometry.
Thus:

gravitational area occurs before areal radius.

The enclosing spherical area defines the areal radius; curvature changes its relation to the local proper ruler. [PDF closing line clipped; author review required.]

title: Addendum 42 — Gravitational Retention Occurs Before Schwarzschild Geometry
section: Abstract
text:
Abstract
Schwarzschild geometry is conventionally introduced as the static, spherically symmetric vacuum solution of Einstein’s field equation:
\[ds^2=-\left(1-\frac{2GM}{c^2r}\right)c^2dt^2+\left(1-\frac{2GM}{c^2r}\right)^{-1}dr^2+r^2d\Omega^2.\]
Recursively Realized Distinguishability (R²D) places this metric late in the logical sequence.
Addendum 35 established that clock and ruler coordinates are projections of an enclosing reference relation.
Addendum 37 distinguished free fall from local support and identified gravity with changing enclosing reference rather than local proper acceleration.
Addendum 38 placed differential free-fall motion before curvature.
Addendum 39 obtained the Einstein equation as the minimal covariant compatibility relation within a specified four-dimensional metric projection class.
Addendum 40 then returned to the weak-field empirical regime and derived
\[\frac{d^2\mathbf r}{dt^2}=-\mu_G\frac{\mathbf r}{r^3},\]
from Keplerian closure, where
\[\mu_G=\frac{4\pi^2a^3}{T^2}.\]
is the directly readable shared gravitational calibration.
Addendum 41 showed that under spherical projection the prior enclosing geometric read is area,
\[A_G,\]
with areal radius defined only afterward:

\[r_A=\sqrt{\frac{A_G}{4\pi}}.\]
It introduced the area-first compactness
\[\chi_G\equiv\frac{2\mu_G}{c^2r_A}=\frac{2\mu_G}{c^2}\sqrt{\frac{4\pi}{A_G}}.\]
The present addendum asks what clock-ruler geometry this compactness acquires under the mature metric projection.
Take the static spherically symmetric exterior metric in areal coordinates,
\[ds^2=-N^2(r_A)c^2dt^2+H^2(r_A)dr_A^2+r_A^2d\Omega^2.\]
In vacuum, with vanishing cosmological constant, the Einstein equation derived in Addendum 39 gives
\[\frac d{dr_A}\left[r_A(1-H^{-2})\right]=0.\]
and
\[\frac d{dr_A}\ln(NH)=0.\]
Hence,
\[H^{-2}=1-\frac{r_s}{r_A},\]
and asymptotic flatness gives
\[NH=1.\]
Therefore,
\[N^2=1-\frac{r_s}{r_A}.\]
The remaining integration constant is fixed by the weak-field Kepler relation. Matching to
\[g_G=\frac{\mu_G}{r_A^2}\]
gives
\[r_s=\frac{2\mu_G}{c^2}.\]
Thus

\[N^2=1-\chi_G=1-\frac{2\mu_G}{c^2r_A}.\]
The exterior geometry is therefore
\[ds^2=-(1-\chi_G)c^2dt^2+(1-\chi_G)^{-1}dr_A^2+r_A^2d\Omega^2.\]
Only after the conventional source calibration
\[\mu_G=GM.\]
does this become the familiar Schwarzschild form.
R²D now supplies a prior count relation.
Let PG denote the compatible gravitational possibility relevant to the exterior-directed read and RG the retained part. Define
\[q_G\equiv\frac{R_G}{P_G},\]
and the normalized residual exterior-readable fraction
\[\alpha_G\equiv\frac{P_G-R_G}{P_G}.\]
Then
\[q_G+\alpha_G=1.\]
The Schwarzschild solution supplies the physical calibration
\[\alpha_G=N=\sqrt{1-\chi_G}.\]
Therefore,
\[q_G=1-\sqrt{1-\chi_G}.\]
The primitive partition remains linear:
\[q_G+\alpha_G=1.\]
The nonlinear relation to compactness appears only in the metric projection:
\[\chi_G=2q_G-q_G^2.\]
For weak gravity,

\[q_G=\frac{\mu_G}{c^2r_A}+O\!\left(\frac{\mu_G^2}{c^4r_A^2}\right).\]
Using the local rest-energy calibration from Addendum 36,
\[E_0=mc^2,\]
the leading retained energetic read becomes
\[q_Gmc^2\simeq\frac{\mu_Gm}{r_A},\]
which is the magnitude of the Newtonian gravitational binding/work coordinate.
At
\[\chi_G=1,\]
the static lapse vanishes:
\[\alpha_G=0.\]
Hence,
\[q_G=1.\]
Under the R²D mapping, the Schwarzschild horizon is therefore complete retention of the selected exterior static read:
\[R_G=P_G.\]
But the boundary has not disappeared.
Its enclosing area remains finite:
\[A_H=\frac{16\pi\mu_G^2}{c^4}.\]
Only afterward does the horizon areal radius follow:
\[r_H=\sqrt{\frac{A_H}{4\pi}}=\frac{2\mu_G}{c^2}.\]
The horizon is therefore area first.
For a static local clock,
\[\frac{d\tau}{dt}=N=\alpha_G.\]

On a static spatial slice,
\[\frac{d\ell_r}{dr_A}=H=\frac1{\alpha_G}.\]
Thus
\[\frac{d\tau}{dt}\frac{d\ell_r}{dr_A}=1.\]
The reciprocal clock-ruler structure that the earlier R²D development sought is therefore not an additional assumption here. It is a consequence of the static spherical vacuum metric projection.
At the horizon,
\[\frac{d\tau}{dt}\longrightarrow0,\]
while
\[\frac{d\ell_r}{dr_A}\longrightarrow\infty.\]
This is the breakdown of the static exterior coordinate decomposition.
It is not destruction of local realization.
A freely falling observer has zero proper acceleration and crosses the horizon without encountering a local curvature singularity. A static observer, by contrast, requires proper support acceleration
\[a_{\mathrm{support}}=\frac{\mu_G}{r_A^2\sqrt{1-\chi_G}},\]
which diverges as
\[\chi_G\longrightarrow1.\]
The divergence belongs to the differential constraint required to prevent free fall.
It is not an infinite primitive gravitational force.
Thus the Schwarzschild solution contains two complementary reads already anticipated by R²D:

free fall = common gravitational realization,

whereas

static support = differential local constraint.


The central claim is therefore:

gravitational retention occurs before Schwarzschild geometry.

More precisely:
the R²D possibility-retention partition exists before metric geometry; Schwarzschild geometry supp

They belong to different logical levels.

section: Abstract

Abstract
The Bekenstein–Hawking relation is conventionally written
\[S_H=\frac{A_H}{4\ell_P^2},\]
where
\[\ell_P^2=\frac{\hbar G}{c^3}.\]
This form invites a geometric interpretation in which a black-hole horizon possesses a physical surface area that is divided into Planck-sized elements, with the resulting number identified as entropy.
Recursively Realized Distinguishability (R²D) reverses that explanatory order.
A horizon is first a boundary-defined count domain. Within that count domain, macrostates are distinguishable and possess multiplicities
\[W_{H,i},\]
with logarithmic count coordinates
\[S_{H,i}=\ln W_{H,i}.\]
The boundary itself acquires a gravitational area projection,
\[A_i,\]
while the distinguishability between radially ordered macrostates acquires a radial projection,
\[r_i.\]
Thus area and radius do not play the same primitive role:

boundary \(\longrightarrow\) area,

whereas


distinguishability \(\longrightarrow\) radius.

This addendum considers the hypothesis that one adjacent radial macrostate distinction receives the physical calibration
\[\Delta r=\ell_P.\]
Planck length is then not a constituent of pre-existing space. It is the radial physical read of one distinguishable macrostate interval.
For spherical Schwarzschild projection,
\[A_i=4\pi r_i^2.\]

\[S_{H,i}=\ln W_{H,i}=\frac{A_i}{4\ell_P^2}.\]
Therefore, for adjacent Planck-distinguished radial macrostates,
\[\ln\frac{W_{H,i+1}}{W_{H,i}}=\frac{A_{i+1}-A_i}{4\ell_P^2}.\]
Under complete-retention proportional realization,
\[\Delta P_{H,i}=\Delta R_{H,i},\]
so the local asymmetry vanishes and the relative occupancy structure reproduces the relative multiplicity structure:
\[\frac{c_{H,i+1}}{c_{H,i}}\approx\frac{W_{H,i+1}}{W_{H,i}}.\]
Hence
\[\frac{c_{H,i+1}}{c_{H,i}}\approx\exp\!\left[\frac{A_{i+1}-A_i}{4\ell_P^2}\right].\]
The exponential is therefore first a relative count relation. Probability appears only after normalization.
If
\[r_i=i\ell_P,\]
then
\[A_i=4\pi i^2\ell_P^2,\]

and one radial macrostate step gives
\[\Delta S_{H,i}=\pi(2i+1).\]
Summing these logarithmic occupancy or multiplicity increments across the radially distinguishable horizon domain gives
\[\sum_{i=0}^{N-1}\Delta S_{H,i}=\pi\sum_{i=0}^{N-1}(2i+1)=\pi N^2.\]
Because
\[r_H=N\ell_P,\]
this becomes
\[S_H=\pi\frac{r_H^2}{\ell_P^2}.\]
The spherical boundary projection is
\[A_H=4\pi r_H^2.\]
Therefore,
\[S_H=\frac{A_H}{4\ell_P^2}.\]
This is not presented as an independent derivation of the Bekenstein–Hawking law, because its area– multiplicity calibration has been used as physical input. Instead, the construction exposes what that law means in the R²D architecture.
The horizon “area” is the geometric read of a boundary-defined count domain. Radius is the read of distinguishability within that domain. Planck length calibrates the distinction between neighboring radial macrostates. The Bekenstein–Hawking exponential defines their relative multiplicities, and at complete retention those relative multiplicities are realized as relative occupancies.
Thus the horizon is not fundamentally tiled by Planck areas.
It is a recursively realized count domain whose mature Schwarzschild projection is area.
Therefore:

horizon multiplicity occurs before Planck-area calibration.

And more specifically:

Schwarzschild area is the geometric projection of a count domain [PDF abstract closing line clipped; author review required.]

title: Addendum 43 — Horizon Multiplicity Occurs Before Planck-Area Calibration
section: 2. Complete Retention Is Not Horizon Multiplicity
text:
2. Complete Retention Is Not Horizon Multiplicity
Retention and multiplicity answer different questions.
Retention asks how much of an enclosing directional relation remains readable as retained distinguishability.

Multiplicity asks how many compatible realizations belong to a macrostate.
Thus
\[R_H\ne W_H.\]
Likewise,
\[q_H\ne S_H.\]
Every Schwarzschild horizon satisfies
\[q_H=1,\]
while Schwarzschild horizon entropy varies with the gravitational mass scale.
Complete retention therefore does not determine multiplicity.

title: Addendum 43 — Horizon Multiplicity Occurs Before Planck-Area Calibration
section: 3. The Horizon Is First a Count Boundary
text:
3. The Horizon Is First a Count Boundary
Let
\[B_H\]
denote the horizon boundary.
The boundary defines a count domain
\[D_H.\]
Within that domain are readable horizon macrostates
\[i\in\mathcal M_H.\]
Each macrostate possesses multiplicity
\[W_{H,i}.\]
Its entropy coordinate is
\[S_{H,i}=\ln W_{H,i}.\]
The multiplicity landscape belongs to the boundary-defined count domain.
It is not created by the later geometric coordinate used to represent the boundary.

title: Addendum 43 — Horizon Multiplicity Occurs Before Planck-Area Calibration
section: 4. Boundary and Distinguishability Have Different Physical Reads
text:
4. Boundary and Distinguishability Have Different Physical Reads
A central distinction is required.
The horizon boundary receives the gravitational geometric read
\[B_H\longrightarrow A_H.\]
A distinction between radially ordered macrostates receives the radial coordinate read
\[\lambda_{H,i\to k}\longrightarrow\Delta r_{i\to k}.\]
Thus area and radius do not arise from the same primitive quantity.
Area reads the boundary.
Radius reads distinguishability.
This is the R²D meaning of area before radius.

title: Addendum 43 — Horizon Multiplicity Occurs Before Planck-Area Calibration
section: 5. Area Is Not Primitive Surface Substance
text:
5. Area Is Not Primitive Surface Substance
The Schwarzschild quantity
\[A_H\]
is a mature gravitational coordinate.
R²D does not require the primitive horizon to be a two-dimensional material surface.
The prior object is the count domain defined by the horizon boundary.
Thus
\[D_H\longrightarrow A_H,\]
not
\[A_H\longrightarrow D_H.\]
The geometric area is how the boundary becomes readable in the Schwarzschild projection.

title: Addendum 43 — Horizon Multiplicity Occurs Before Planck-Area Calibration
section: 6. Radial Macrostates Are Distinctions Within the Count Domain
text:
6. Radial Macrostates Are Distinctions Within the Count Domain
Now consider an ordered family of horizon macrostates
\[i=0,1,2,\ldots.\]
The labels do not identify physical material shells.
They identify distinguishable alternatives within the horizon count domain.
Let adjacent macrostates satisfy
\[i\longrightarrow i+1.\]
The physical radial read of that distinction is
\[\Delta r_i.\]
crumbs: Addenda

title: Addendum 43 — Horizon Multiplicity Occurs Before Planck-Area Calibration
section: 7. Candidate Planck Radial Calibration
text:
7. Candidate Planck Radial Calibration
The hypothesis explored here is
\[\Delta r_i=\ell_P\]
for one elementary adjacent radial distinction.
Thus
\[r_i=i\ell_P\]
relative to the chosen radial reference.
This does not mean that background space is constructed from Planck-length segments.
It means

one macrostate distinction \(\longrightarrow\ell_P\)

under the quantum–gravitational radial calibration.
The count distinction remains prior.
crumbs: Addenda

title: Addendum 43 — Horizon Multiplicity Occurs Before Planck-Area Calibration
section: 8. Planck Length and Planck Area Must Not Be Confused
text:
8. Planck Length and Planck Area Must Not Be Confused
Planck length is
\[\ell_P=\sqrt{\frac{\hbar G}{c^3}}.\]
Planck area is
\[\ell_P^2=\frac{\hbar G}{c^3}.\]
In the present construction these enter different projected relations.
The radial distinction is calibrated through
\[\ell_P.\]
The boundary multiplicity is calibrated against area through
\[\ell_P^2.\]
Thus

\(\ell_P\longleftrightarrow\) radial distinction,

whereas

\(\ell_P^2\longleftrightarrow\) areal multiplicity calibration.

Neither is assumed to be a primitive constituent of space.
crumbs: Addenda

title: Addendum 43 — Horizon Multiplicity Occurs Before Planck-Area Calibration
section: 9. Spherical Projection Assigns an Area to Each Radial Macrostate
text:
9. Spherical Projection Assigns an Area to Each Radial Macrostate
Under spherical symmetry,
\[A_i=4\pi r_i^2.\]
Using
\[r_i=i\ell_P,\]
gives
\[A_i=4\pi i^2\ell_P^2.\]

This area is the boundary-coordinate read associated with radial macrostate i.
crumbs: Addenda

title: Addendum 43 — Horizon Multiplicity Occurs Before Planck-Area Calibration
section: 10. Bekenstein–Hawking Supplies the Multiplicity Calibration
text:
10. Bekenstein–Hawking Supplies the Multiplicity Calibration
The physical Bekenstein–Hawking relation is
\[S_{H,i}=\frac{A_i}{4\ell_P^2}.\]
R²D separately defines
\[S_{H,i}=\ln W_{H,i}.\]
Therefore,
\[\ln W_{H,i}=\frac{A_i}{4\ell_P^2}.\]
Equivalently,
\[W_{H,i}=\exp\!\left(\frac{A_i}{4\ell_P^2}\right).\]
This is a physical calibration of multiplicity.
It should not be read causally as area creating states.
crumbs: Addenda

title: Addendum 43 — Horizon Multiplicity Occurs Before Planck-Area Calibration
section: 11. The Logical Direction Remains Count First
text:
11. The Logical Direction Remains Count First
The conventional reading can suggest
\[A_i\longrightarrow S_i\longrightarrow W_i.\]
R²D reverses the ontology.
The primitive order is
\[B_H\longrightarrow W_{H,i}\longrightarrow S_{H,i},\]
followed by the physical correspondence
\[S_{H,i}\longleftrightarrow\frac{A_i}{4\ell_P^2}.\]

Area calibrates the gravitational read of the count.
It does not cause the count.
crumbs: Addenda

title: Addendum 43 — Horizon Multiplicity Occurs Before Planck-Area Calibration
section: 12. Adjacent Horizon Macrostates Have a Multiplicity Ratio
text:
12. Adjacent Horizon Macrostates Have a Multiplicity Ratio
For two neighboring radial macrostates,
\[i\quad\text{and}\quad i+1,\]
their entropy difference is
\[\Delta S_{H,i}=S_{H,i+1}-S_{H,i}.\]
Therefore,
\[\Delta S_{H,i}=\ln\frac{W_{H,i+1}}{W_{H,i}}.\]
Using the physical area calibration,
\[\Delta S_{H,i}=\frac{A_{i+1}-A_i}{4\ell_P^2}.\]
Hence
\[\frac{W_{H,i+1}}{W_{H,i}}=\exp\!\left[\frac{\Delta A_i}{4\ell_P^2}\right].\]
crumbs: Addenda

title: Addendum 43 — Horizon Multiplicity Occurs Before Planck-Area Calibration
section: 13. The Exponential Is First a Count Ratio
text:
13. The Exponential Is First a Count Ratio
The relation
\[\frac{W_{H,i+1}}{W_{H,i}}=e^{\Delta S_{H,i}}.\]
contains no probability assumption.
It follows immediately from
\[S=\ln W.\]
Thus the exponential first restores a multiplicative possible-count ratio from its additive logarithmic coordinate.

Probability can appear only after those counts are normalized.
Therefore:

multiplicity ratio \(\longrightarrow\) normalized probability,

not

probability \(\longrightarrow\) multiplicity.
crumbs: Addenda

title: Addendum 43 — Horizon Multiplicity Occurs Before Planck-Area Calibration
section: 14. This Is the Same Architecture Underlying Boltzmann Weighting
text:
14. This Is the Same Architecture Underlying Boltzmann Weighting
Boltzmann weighting has the generic structure
\[\frac{c_k}{c_i}=e^{\Delta G_{i\to k}},\]
where the exponential restores a multiplicative occupancy ratio from a logarithmic count difference.
The horizon relation has the same count architecture:
\[\frac{W_{H,i+1}}{W_{H,i}}=e^{\Delta A_i/(4\ell_P^2)}.\]
The conventional physical coordinate differs.
The logarithmic-count architecture does not.
crumbs: Addenda

title: Addendum 43 — Horizon Multiplicity Occurs Before Planck-Area Calibration
section: 15. Multiplicity and Occupancy Remain Different Counts
text:
15. Multiplicity and Occupancy Remain Different Counts
Let
\[c_{H,i}\]
denote realized occupancy of horizon macrostate i.
Then generally
\[c_{H,i}\ne W_{H,i}.\]
Multiplicity is possible-count structure.
Occupancy is realized structure.

R²D does not collapse them.
crumbs: Addenda

title: Addendum 43 — Horizon Multiplicity Occurs Before Planck-Area Calibration
section: 16. The General Occupancy Relation
text:
16. The General Occupancy Relation
For a readable macrostate transition,
\[i\longrightarrow i+1,\]
R²D gives
\[\Delta G_{H,i}=\Delta\tau_{H,i}+\Delta A_{H,i},\]
where
\[\Delta G_{H,i}=\ln\frac{c_{H,i+1}}{c_{H,i}}.\]
Under proportional occurrence realization,
\[\Delta\tau_{H,i}\approx\Delta S_{H,i}.\]
Therefore,
\[\Delta G_{H,i}\approx\Delta S_{H,i}+\Delta A_{H,i}.\]

title: Addendum 43 — Horizon Multiplicity Occurs Before Planck-Area Calibration
section: 17. Equilibrium Removes the Directional Occupancy Bias
text:
17. Equilibrium Removes the Directional Occupancy Bias
For the stationary complete-retention branch considered here, suppose the adjacent radial macrostate comparison satisfies
\[\Delta P_{H,i}=\Delta R_{H,i}.\]
Then
\[\Delta A_{H,i}=0.\]
Therefore,
\[\Delta G_{H,i}\approx\Delta S_{H,i}.\]
Thus
\[\ln\frac{c_{H,i+1}}{c_{H,i}}\approx\ln\frac{W_{H,i+1}}{W_{H,i}}.\]

Exponentiating,
\[\frac{c_{H,i+1}}{c_{H,i}}\approx\frac{W_{H,i+1}}{W_{H,i}}.\]
This is the precise sense in which the equilibrium horizon occupancy realizes its multiplicity landscape.
crumbs: Addenda

section: 18. The Horizon Occupancy Ratio Is Therefore Area-Calibrated
text:
18. The Horizon Occupancy Ratio Is Therefore Area-Calibrated
Using the Bekenstein–Hawking physical calibration,
\[\frac{c_{H,i+1}}{c_{H,i}}\approx\exp\!\left[\frac{A_{i+1}-A_i}{4\ell_P^2}\right].\]
The right-hand side is first a relative count weight.
Normalization is still not required.

title: Addendum 43 — Horizon Multiplicity Occurs Before Planck-Area Calibration
section: 19. The Planck-Distinguished Radial Landscape Gives an Exact Finite Increment
text:
19. The Planck-Distinguished Radial Landscape Gives an Exact Finite Increment
Using
\[r_i=i\ell_P,\]
the associated projected area is
\[A_i=4\pi i^2\ell_P^2.\]
Therefore,
\[\Delta A_i=A_{i+1}-A_i\]
is
\[\Delta A_i=4\pi\ell_P^2\left[(i+1)^2-i^2\right].\]
Thus
\[\Delta A_i=4\pi\ell_P^2(2i+1).\]
crumbs: Addenda

title: Addendum 43 — Horizon Multiplicity Occurs Before Planck-Area Calibration
section: 20. The Corresponding Logarithmic Multiplicity Increment
text:
20. The Corresponding Logarithmic Multiplicity Increment
Divide by
\[4\ell_P^2.\]
Then
\[\Delta S_{H,i}=\pi(2i+1).\]
Therefore,
\[\frac{W_{H,i+1}}{W_{H,i}}=e^{\pi(2i+1)}.\]
And in the complete-retention proportional-realization limit,
\[\frac{c_{H,i+1}}{c_{H,i}}\approx e^{\pi(2i+1)}.\]
This is the discrete radial horizon occupancy relation.
crumbs: Addenda

title: Addendum 43 — Horizon Multiplicity Occurs Before Planck-Area Calibration
section: 21. Nothing Has Been Assigned to a Midpoint State
text:
21. Nothing Has Been Assigned to a Midpoint State
The result follows directly from
\[i\longrightarrow i+1.\]
There is no macrostate
\[i+\frac12.\]
There is no half boundary.
There is no additional radial coordinate.
The term
\[2i+1\]
appears only because
\[(i+1)^2-i^2=2i+1.\]
It is the exact finite difference of the spherical area projection between two adjacent radial macrostates.
crumbs: Addenda

title: Addendum 43 — Horizon Multiplicity Occurs Before Planck-Area Calibration
section: 22. The Horizon Count Accumulates Across the Radial Macrostates
text:
22. The Horizon Count Accumulates Across the Radial Macrostates
Sum the logarithmic multiplicity increments:
\[\sum_{i=0}^{N-1}\Delta S_{H,i}.\]
Using
\[\Delta S_{H,i}=\pi(2i+1),\]
gives
\[\sum_{i=0}^{N-1}\Delta S_{H,i}=\pi\sum_{i=0}^{N-1}(2i+1).\]
The odd integers satisfy
\[\sum_{i=0}^{N-1}(2i+1)=N^2.\]
Therefore,
\[\sum_{i=0}^{N-1}\Delta S_{H,i}=\pi N^2.\]
crumbs: Addenda
24  Addendum 43 — Horizon Multiplicity Occurs Before Planck-Area Calibration

title: Addendum 43 — Horizon Multiplicity Occurs Before Planck-Area Calibration
section: 23. The Same Sum Is a Telescoping Multiplicity Relation
text:
23. The Same Sum Is a Telescoping Multiplicity Relation
Because
\[\Delta S_{H,i}=\ln\frac{W_{H,i+1}}{W_{H,i}},\]
we have
\[\sum_{i=0}^{N-1}\Delta S_{H,i}=\sum_{i=0}^{N-1}\ln\frac{W_{H,i+1}}{W_{H,i}}.\]
Therefore,

\[\sum_{i=0}^{N-1}\Delta S_{H,i}=\ln\frac{W_{H,N}}{W_{H,0}}.\]
The intermediate multiplicities cancel as ratios.
This is an accumulated count relation.
crumbs: Addenda
24  Addendum 43 — Horizon Multiplicity Occurs Before Planck-Area Calibration

title: Addendum 43 — Horizon Multiplicity Occurs Before Planck-Area Calibration
section: 24. At Equilibrium the Same Sum Is Read Through Occupancy
text:
24. At Equilibrium the Same Sum Is Read Through Occupancy
Under complete-retention proportional realization,
\[\Delta G_{H,i}\approx\Delta S_{H,i}.\]
Therefore,
\[\sum_{i=0}^{N-1}\Delta G_{H,i}\approx\sum_{i=0}^{N-1}\Delta S_{H,i}.\]
Since
\[\Delta G_{H,i}=\ln\frac{c_{H,i+1}}{c_{H,i}},\]
the occupancy ratios telescope:
\[\ln\frac{c_{H,N}}{c_{H,0}}\approx\pi N^2.\]
Thus the accumulated logarithmic occupancy difference across the radially distinguishable macrostate domain realizes the accumulated multiplicity difference.
crumbs: Addenda
24  Addendum 43 — Horizon Multiplicity Occurs Before Planck-Area Calibration

title: Addendum 43 — Horizon Multiplicity Occurs Before Planck-Area Calibration
section: 25. This Is the Relevant Sense in Which Occupancy Is Summed Across Radius
text:
25. This Is the Relevant Sense in Which Occupancy Is Summed Across Radius
The primitive construction is not
\[A_H=\sum_i c_i.\]
Raw occupancies are not areas.
Rather, the additive quantity is the logarithmic occupancy difference:

\[\sum_i\ln\frac{c_{i+1}}{c_i}.\]
At equilibrium this reproduces
\[\sum_i\ln\frac{W_{i+1}}{W_i}.\]
The latter is the accumulated horizon entropy difference.
Thus Schwarzschild area is the geometric read of the boundary whose radially organized occupancy structure realizes this count landscape.
crumbs: Addenda
24  Addendum 43 — Horizon Multiplicity Occurs Before Planck-Area Calibration

title: Addendum 43 — Horizon Multiplicity Occurs Before Planck-Area Calibration
section: 26. Recover the Horizon Radius
text:
26. Recover the Horizon Radius
After N radial macrostate distinctions,
\[r_H=N\ell_P.\]
Therefore,
\[N=\frac{r_H}{\ell_P}.\]
The accumulated count becomes
\[S_H=\pi N^2,\]
or
\[S_H=\pi\frac{r_H^2}{\ell_P^2}.\]
crumbs: Addenda

title: Addendum 43 — Horizon Multiplicity Occurs Before Planck-Area Calibration
section: 27. The Boundary Projection Gives the Factor Four
text:
27. The Boundary Projection Gives the Factor Four
The same count boundary is represented geometrically by
\[A_H=4\pi r_H^2.\]
Therefore,
\[\pi r_H^2=\frac{A_H}{4}.\]
Hence

\[S_H=\frac{A_H}{4\ell_P^2}.\]
The factor four appears when the radial distinguishability coordinate is mapped onto the spherical boundary projection.
It does not require four microscopic area tiles per entropy unit.
crumbs: Addenda

title: Addendum 43 — Horizon Multiplicity Occurs Before Planck-Area Calibration
section: 28. The π Is Part of the Spherical Area Relation
text:
28. The π Is Part of the Spherical Area Relation
The remaining π is not introduced as an entropy circumference.
It enters because the boundary projection is spherical:
\[A=4\pi r^2.\]
When that area relation is divided by four,
\[\frac A4=\pi r^2.\]
Therefore
\[S=\pi\left(\frac r{\ell_P}\right)^2.\]
The π belongs to the area–radius projection.
It is not a new primitive R²D occurrence relation.
crumbs: Addenda
24  Addendum 43 — Horizon Multiplicity Occurs Before Planck-Area Calibration

title: Addendum 43 — Horizon Multiplicity Occurs Before Planck-Area Calibration
section: 29. This Is Not Planck-Area Tiling
text:
29. This Is Not Planck-Area Tiling
The construction contains no primitive statement that the horizon is composed of cells having area
\[\ell_P^2\]
or
\[4\ell_P^2.\]
Instead:
\[\Delta r=\ell_P\]
calibrates distinguishability,

while
\[S=\frac A{4\ell_P^2}\]
calibrates multiplicity against the boundary-area projection.
These are different mappings.
crumbs: Addenda

title: Addendum 43 — Horizon Multiplicity Occurs Before Planck-Area Calibration
section: 30. One Additional Microstate Is Not One Planck Area
text:
30. One Additional Microstate Is Not One Planck Area
Suppose a horizon macrostate has multiplicity W .
Adding one compatible realization would give
\[W\longrightarrow W+1.\]
The entropy change is
\[\Delta S=\ln\!\left(1+\frac1W\right).\]
Therefore its Bekenstein–Hawking area read would be
\[\Delta A=4\ell_P^2\ln\!\left(1+\frac1W\right).\]
For
\[W\gg1,\]
\[\Delta A\approx\frac{4\ell_P^2}{W}.\]
Thus one additional compatible realization does not correspond to one fixed Planck-area patch.
This independently excludes the literal-tile interpretation.
crumbs: Addenda
24  Addendum 43 — Horizon Multiplicity Occurs Before Planck-Area Calibration

title: Addendum 43 — Horizon Multiplicity Occurs Before Planck-Area Calibration
section: 31. One Nat Is Also Not One Planck-Length Step
text:
31. One Nat Is Also Not One Planck-Length Step
A one-nat multiplicity change is
\[\Delta S=1.\]
But the Planck radial macrostate step at index i has

\[\Delta S_i=\pi(2i+1).\]
Therefore
\[\Delta S=1\;\not\Rightarrow\;\Delta r=\ell_P.\quad\text{[PDF callout glyph clipped; author review required.]}\]
The radial count radix and the logarithmic multiplicity radix are different quantities.
This distinction is necessary for the later gravitational well-depth analysis.
crumbs: Addenda

title: Addendum 43 — Horizon Multiplicity Occurs Before Planck-Area Calibration
section: 32. Normalization Produces a Horizon Probability Distribution
text:
32. Normalization Produces a Horizon Probability Distribution
Before normalization the relative horizon weights are
\[W_{H,i}=\exp\!\left(\frac{A_i}{4\ell_P^2}\right).\]
If a normalized macrostate probability is desired, define
\[Z_H=\sum_jW_{H,j}.\]
Then
\[p_{H,i}=\frac{W_{H,i}}{Z_H}=\frac{\exp[A_i/(4\ell_P^2)]}{\sum_j\exp[A_j/(4\ell_P^2)]}.\]
The normalized probability distribution therefore appears after the multiplicity landscape has already been defined.
crumbs: Addenda
24  Addendum 43 — Horizon Multiplicity Occurs Before Planck-Area Calibration

title: Addendum 43 — Horizon Multiplicity Occurs Before Planck-Area Calibration
section: 33. The Boltzmann Architecture Is Now Explicit
text:
33. The Boltzmann Architecture Is Now Explicit
The sequence is

boundary-defined multiplicity


\(\Downarrow\)

\[S_i=\ln W_i\]

\(\Downarrow\)

\[W_i=e^{S_i}\]

\(\Downarrow\)


\[c_i\propto W_i\]
at complete-retention proportional realization,
followed only afterward by
\[p_i=\frac{c_i}{\sum_jc_j}.\]
This is the same primitive statistical order underlying Boltzmann weighting.
crumbs: Addenda

title: Addendum 43 — Horizon Multiplicity Occurs Before Planck-Area Calibration
section: 34. The Atmosphere Is the Closest Readable Analogue
text:
34. The Atmosphere Is the Closest Readable Analogue
In an isothermal atmosphere, height labels distinguishable spatial macrostates.
Their equilibrium occupancy obeys
\[\frac{c(z_2)}{c(z_1)}=\exp\!\left[-\frac{mg(z_2-z_1)}{k_BT}\right].\]
The exponential does not create the atmospheric occupancy landscape.
It restores a multiplicative occupancy ratio from a logarithmic thermodynamic coordinate.
The horizon relation has the same architecture:
\[\frac{c_{i+1}}{c_i}\approx\exp\!\left[\frac{\Delta A_i}{4\ell_P^2}\right].\]
In both cases, spatially distinguishable macrostates are occupied according to a larger equilibrium count relation.
crumbs: Addenda
24  Addendum 43 — Horizon Multiplicity Occurs Before Planck-Area Calibration

title: Addendum 43 — Horizon Multiplicity Occurs Before Planck-Area Calibration
section: 35. The Physical Coordinates Are Different
text:
35. The Physical Coordinates Are Different
The atmospheric macrostate coordinate is read directly as height.
The horizon boundary is instead in the gravitational readability regime.
The boundary itself is read through area,
while its internal distinguishability is read radially.
Thus:


atmosphere: distinguishability \(\longrightarrow z\),

whereas

horizon: boundary \(\longrightarrow A\), distinguishability \(\longrightarrow r\).

The statistical architecture remains the same.
crumbs: Addenda
24  Addendum 43 — Horizon Multiplicity Occurs Before Planck-Area Calibration

title: Addendum 43 — Horizon Multiplicity Occurs Before Planck-Area Calibration
section: 36. The Horizon Does Not Store a Labelled Catalogue
text:
36. The Horizon Does Not Store a Labelled Catalogue
The multiplicity
\[W_H\]
does not require the horizon to store an independently readable label for every subordinate realization.
Recursive replacement removes subordinate path identity.
What remains countable is the degeneracy consequence.
Therefore,

subordinate identities lost \(\not\Rightarrow\) multiplicity lost. [PDF callout clipped; author review required.]

A horizon macrostate may possess enormous multiplicity even though its subordinate realization paths are unreadable from the enclosing boundary.
crumbs: Addenda
24  Addendum 43 — Horizon Multiplicity Occurs Before Planck-Area Calibration

title: Addendum 43 — Horizon Multiplicity Occurs Before Planck-Area Calibration
section: 37. Horizon Entropy Is Not Background
text:
37. Horizon Entropy Is Not Background
The horizon state entropy is
\[S_H=\ln W_H.\]
R²D background is a different count relation,
\[\Phi_H=\ln b_H.\]
Therefore,
\[S_H\ne\Phi_H.\]
Likewise horizon state entropy is not automatically entropy production:

\[S_H\ne\delta\Phi_H.\]
A stationary horizon can possess large state multiplicity without producing Second-Law background merely by existing.
crumbs: Addenda
24  Addendum 43 — Horizon Multiplicity Occurs Before Planck-Area Calibration

title: Addendum 43 — Horizon Multiplicity Occurs Before Planck-Area Calibration
section: 38. Horizon Entropy Is Not Retention
text:
38. Horizon Entropy Is Not Retention
Likewise,
\[S_H\ne R_H.\]
At a Schwarzschild horizon,
\[P_H=R_H\]
describes complete retention of the selected static exterior relation.
It does not state the number of compatible horizon realizations.
Retention and multiplicity remain different primitive count relations.
crumbs: Addenda
24  Addendum 43 — Horizon Multiplicity Occurs Before Planck-Area Calibration

title: Addendum 43 — Horizon Multiplicity Occurs Before Planck-Area Calibration
section: 39. Insert the Schwarzschild Horizon Area
text:
39. Insert the Schwarzschild Horizon Area
From Addendum 42,
\[A_H=\frac{16\pi\mu_G^2}{c^4}.\]
Therefore,
\[S_H=\frac{16\pi\mu_G^2/c^4}{4\ell_P^2}.\]
Using
\[\ell_P^2=\frac{\hbar G}{c^3},\]
gives
\[S_H=\frac{4\pi\mu_G^2}{\hbar Gc}.\]
Thus

\[W_H=\exp\!\left(\frac{4\pi\mu_G^2}{\hbar Gc}\right).\]
crumbs: Addenda
24  Addendum 43 — Horizon Multiplicity Occurs Before Planck-Area Calibration

title: Addendum 43 — Horizon Multiplicity Occurs Before Planck-Area Calibration
section: 40. Only Then Apply the Source Calibration
text:
40. Only Then Apply the Source Calibration
With
\[\mu_G=GM,\]
we obtain
\[S_H=\frac{4\pi GM^2}{\hbar c}.\]
Therefore,
\[W_H=\exp\!\left(\frac{4\pi GM^2}{\hbar c}\right).\]
This is the effective Schwarzschild horizon multiplicity implied by the semiclassical entropy calibration.
crumbs: Addenda
24  Addendum 43 — Horizon Multiplicity Occurs Before Planck-Area Calibration

title: Addendum 43 — Horizon Multiplicity Occurs Before Planck-Area Calibration
section: 41. The Effective Multiplicity Need Not Be a Literal Integer Model
text:
41. The Effective Multiplicity Need Not Be a Literal Integer Model
The Bekenstein–Hawking relation is semiclassical.
For arbitrary continuously parameterized M , the expression
\[W_H=e^{S_H}\]
should therefore be interpreted here as the effective multiplicity represented by the calibrated entropy.

50. Conclusion
A Schwarzschild horizon should not be interpreted primitively as a surface tiled by Planck-area elements.
R²D begins one level earlier.
The horizon is a count boundary.
That boundary defines a domain of distinguishable macrostates.
The boundary itself is physically read through area:
\[B_H\longrightarrow A_H.\]
Differences among radially ordered macrostates are physically read through radius:
\[\lambda_H\longrightarrow r_A.\]
The possibility explored here is that one elementary radial distinction receives the physical calibration
\[\Delta r=\ell_P.\]
The Bekenstein–Hawking relation then supplies the physical multiplicity calibration
\[\ln W_i=\frac{A_i}{4\ell_P^2}.\]
For adjacent radial macrostates,
\[\frac{W_{i+1}}{W_i}=\exp\!\left[\frac{\Delta A_i}{4\ell_P^2}\right].\]
At complete retention, R²D proportional realization gives
\[\frac{c_{i+1}}{c_i}\approx\frac{W_{i+1}}{W_i}.\]
Thus the Bekenstein–Hawking exponential can be read as an equilibrium macrostate occupancy relation across a radially distinguished horizon count domain.
With
\[r_i=i\ell_P,\]
the spherical boundary projection gives
\[A_i=4\pi i^2\ell_P^2,\]
so

\[S_i=\pi i^2,\]
and one radial step gives
\[\Delta S_i=\pi(2i+1).\]
Accumulating across the radial macrostate domain,
\[\sum_{i=0}^{N-1}\Delta S_i=\pi N^2.\]
Because
\[r_H=N\ell_P,\]
this becomes
\[S_H=\pi\frac{r_H^2}{\ell_P^2}.\]
The same boundary is represented spherically by
\[A_H=4\pi r_H^2.\]
Therefore,
\[S_H=\frac{A_H}{4\ell_P^2}.\]
The factor four is therefore not evidence for four microscopic Planck-area pieces.
It is the relation between the radial distinguishability projection and the spherical boundary projection.
The area does not create the multiplicity.
The radius does not create the macrostates.
The Planck scale does not create the count domain.
The order is
boundary → count domain → macrostate distinction → multiplicity → occupancy → radial and areal projection.
Thus:

horizon multiplicity occurs before Planck-area calibration.

More specifically:

The Schwarzschild horizon area is the spherical projection of a boundary-defined count domain [PDF closing line clipped; author review required.]

title: Addendum 44 — Entropic-Well Depth Occurs Before Maximum Gravitational Mass
section: Abstract
text:
Abstract
A maximum gravitational mass is ordinarily posed as a property of matter or of a gravitational solution.
Recursively Realized Distinguishability (R²D) begins earlier.
Addendum 43 established that a Schwarzschild horizon can be represented as a boundary-defined count domain containing radially distinguishable macrostates. Their multiplicities are
\[W_{H,i},\]
with logarithmic coordinates
\[S_{H,i}=\ln W_{H,i}.\]
The horizon boundary is physically projected through area,
\[B_H\longrightarrow A_H,\]
while distinguishability within the boundary is projected through radius,
\[\lambda_H\longrightarrow r_H.\]
Under the Bekenstein–Hawking physical calibration,
\[S_H=\frac{A_H}{4\ell_P^2},\]
and under the candidate Planck radial calibration,
\[r_i=i\ell_P.\]
The present addendum asks what it means for such a gravitational multiplicity landscape to become deep, and whether that depth can possess an intrinsic maximum.
Define the depth of a gravitational multiplicity well relative to a reference macrostate by
\[D_H\equiv S_H-S_0=\ln\frac{W_H}{W_0}.\]

For the convenient reference
\[W_0=1,\]
this becomes
\[D_H=S_H.\]
This does not identify horizon entropy with gravitational retention.
Retention and multiplicity remain distinct:
\[R_H\ne S_H.\]
The well depth measures separation in logarithmic multiplicity, not retained possibility.
For the Planck-distinguished radial horizon construction,
\[D_H=\pi N^2,\]
where
\[N=\frac{r_H}{\ell_P}.\]
Under the Schwarzschild mapping
\[r_H=\frac{2GM}{c^2},\]
this becomes
\[D_H=\frac{4\pi GM^2}{\hbar c}.\]
Thus physical gravitational mass is a downstream coordinate of multiplicity-well depth:
\[M=\sqrt{\frac{\hbar c}{4\pi G}}\sqrt{D_H}.\]
Nothing in this relation imposes a maximum value of DH or M .
A maximum gravitational mass therefore cannot be intrinsic to the subordinate well alone.
It requires an enclosing boundary.
Let the subordinate gravitational boundary have multiplicity

\[W_H\]
and let an enclosing gravitational count boundary have multiplicity
\[W_E.\]
Define the subordinate–enclosing multiplicity gap
\[\Delta S_{E\mid H}=S_E-S_H=\ln\frac{W_E}{W_H}.\]
As long as
\[\Delta S_{E\mid H}>0,\]
the subordinate and enclosing count classes remain distinguishable under the nested classification considered here.
The marginal condition is
\[\Delta S_{E\mid H}=0.\]
Then
\[S_E=S_H\]
and therefore
\[W_E=W_H.\]
The multiplicity distinction defining the subordinate/enclosing relation has vanished.
If both gravitational boundaries are read through the same areal multiplicity calibration,
\[S=\frac A{4\ell_P^2},\]
then
\[\Delta S_{E\mid H}=\frac{A_E-A_H}{4\ell_P^2}.\]
Therefore the count-level marginal condition projects physically as
\[A_E=A_H.\]
Maximum gravitational mass is then the later physical source coordinate assigned to this prior loss of subordinate–enclosing multiplicity distinction.

The logical order is therefore
multiplicity well → well depth → enclosing multiplicity gap → gap closure → areal equality → maximum mass.
A formal continuation of the original subordinate/enclosing classification after
\[W_E=W_H\]
would preserve a distinction no longer supported by the defining count relation.
This is the gravitational analogue of a Gibbs-type boundary-classification failure.
The present addendum does not identify the physical solution that realizes this marginal condition.
That is the purpose of Addendum 45.
Its central claim is narrower:

a maximum gravitational mass is not an intrinsic property of a local mass.

Rather,
gravitational mass saturation is the projected physical read of a prior enclosing multiplicity limit.
Thus:

entropic-well depth occurs before maximum gravitational mass.

\[S=\ln W,\]

belongs to horizon retention.

\[W_E=W_H\]
belongs to subordinate–enclosing multiplicity saturation.

section: 23. Saturation Is Not the Schwarzschild Horizon
text:
23. Saturation Is Not the Schwarzschild Horizon
The Schwarzschild horizon is a readability horizon.
The relevant exterior-directed recurrence becomes unreadable while the gravitational boundary remains realized.

Abstract

Let a subordinate gravitational boundary have multiplicity

\[W_c.\]
Define their logarithmic multiplicity gap
\[\Delta S_{c\mid b}=S_c-S_b=\ln\frac{W_c}{W_b}.\]
The nested classification remains multiplicatively distinct while
\[\Delta S_{c\mid b}>0.\]
Its marginal condition is
\[\Delta S_{c\mid b}=0.\]
Then
\[W_b=W_c.\]
If both boundaries share the same horizon-area calibration,
\[S=\frac A{4\ell_P^2},\]
the same condition is physically read as
\[A_b=A_c.\]

Addendum 44 did not identify a physical system that satisfies this relation. It deliberately stopped before assigning a maximum mass.
Schwarzschild–de Sitter geometry provides an exact independent test.
For positive cosmological constant Λ, the static projection is
\[ds^2=-f(r)c^2dt^2+\frac{dr^2}{f(r)}+r^2d\Omega^2,\]
where
\[f(r)=1-\frac{2GM}{c^2r}-\frac{\Lambda r^2}{3}.\]
Within its nonextremal two-horizon regime, the equation
\[f(r)=0\]

\[r_b<r_c,\]

They are not independent surfaces inserted into a fixed container. They are two roots of one shared gravitational equation.
Their exact coupling implies

Define

Then

\[\Delta S_{c\mid b}>0.\]
Thus throughout the ordinary two-horizon Schwarzschild–de Sitter regime,
\[W_c>W_b.\]

\[S_b=S_c,\]

The subordinate area grows while the enclosing area contracts.

\[f(r)=0.\]
Therefore changing M changes both roots.
The black-hole and cosmological horizon reads are not independently variable physical surfaces.
They are coupled solutions of one gravitational relation.
This already matches the structural requirement from Addendum 44:
\[W_H=W_H(M),\]
while
\[W_E=W_E(M,\ldots).\]
The enclosing boundary need not remain fixed while the subordinate well changes.

6. Multiply the Horizon Equation by r
From
\[1-\frac{2GM}{c^2r}-\frac{\Lambda r^2}{3}=0,\]
multiply by r :
\[r-\frac{2GM}{c^2}-\frac{\Lambda r^3}{3}=0.\]
Rearrange:
\[r^3-\frac3\Lambda r+\frac{6GM}{\Lambda c^2}=0.\]
This cubic makes the coupling among the roots explicit.

\[r_n<0.\]
The cubic contains no r 2 term.
Therefore the sum of its roots vanishes:
\[r_b+r_c+r_n=0.\]
Hence,
\[r_n=-(r_b+r_c).\]

text:
8. The Pairwise Root Relation Gives the Coupled Horizon Identity
For the cubic,
\[r_br_c+r_br_n+r_cr_n=-\frac3\Lambda.\]
Substitute
\[r_n=-(r_b+r_c).\]

Then
\[r_br_c-r_b(r_b+r_c)-r_c(r_b+r_c)=-\frac3\Lambda.\]
Simplifying gives
\[-r_b^2-r_br_c-r_c^2=-\frac3\Lambda.\]
Therefore,
\[r_b^2+r_br_c+r_c^2=\frac3\Lambda.\]
This is the exact coupled horizon relation.

At horizon coalescence,

text:
11. Solve the Coupled Horizon Identity
Using q
Write
\[r_b=qr_c.\]
Then
\[q^2r_c^2+qr_c^2+r_c^2=\frac3\Lambda.\]
Therefore,
\[r_c^2(1+q+q^2)=\frac3\Lambda.\]
Hence,
\[r_c^2=\frac3{\Lambda(1+q+q^2)}.\]
And
\[r_b^2=\frac{3q^2}{\Lambda(1+q+q^2)}.\]

Then
\[\sigma_{b\mid c}=q^2.\]
For
\[0\le q<1,\]

At equality,

\[\Delta S_{c\mid b}\equiv S_c-S_b.\]

\[S=\ln W,\]

\[\Delta S_{c\mid b}=\ln\frac{W_c}{W_b}.\]
This is the actual multiplicative distinction between the two horizon classes.

text:
18. Substitute the Exact Coupled Areas

\[A_c=\frac{12\pi}{\Lambda(1+q+q^2)},\]
and
\[A_b=\frac{12\pi q^2}{\Lambda(1+q+q^2)},\]
we obtain
\[\Delta S_{c\mid b}=\frac{A_c-A_b}{4\ell_P^2}.\]
Therefore,
\[\Delta S_{c\mid b}=\frac{3\pi}{\Lambda\ell_P^2}\frac{1-q^2}{1+q+q^2}.\]
Equivalently,
\[\ln\frac{W_c}{W_b}=\frac{3\pi}{\Lambda\ell_P^2}\frac{1-q^2}{1+q+q^2}.\]

For
\[0\le q<1,\]

The denominator
\[1+q+q^2\]
is positive.
Therefore,
\[\Delta S_{c\mid b}>0.\]
Hence,
\[W_c>W_b.\]
The enclosing cosmological horizon remains multiplicatively distinguishable from the subordinate black- hole horizon throughout the ordinary two-horizon regime.

\[A_b\uparrow,\]

In general,

\[S_b=S_c,\]
\[A_b=A_c,\]

\[r_b<r_c.\]

\[\Delta S_{E\mid H}=0\quad\Longrightarrow\quad A_E=A_H.\]
Conventional Exact Physical Input

\[f(r)=1-\frac{2GM}{c^2r}-\frac{\Lambda r^2}{3}.\]

Derived Exact Geometry
The two positive horizon roots satisfy
\[r_b^2+r_br_c+r_c^2=\frac3\Lambda.\]
Defining

gives
\[A_b=\frac{12\pi q^2}{\Lambda(1+q+q^2)},\]
\[A_c=\frac{12\pi}{\Lambda(1+q+q^2)},\]

Derived Multiplicity Gap
Using the common horizon calibration,
\[\Delta S_{c\mid b}=\frac{3\pi}{\Lambda\ell_P^2}\frac{1-q^2}{1+q+q^2}.\]

Independently Derived Maximum

\[r_N=\frac1{\sqrt\Lambda},\]
and
\[M_N=\frac{c^2}{3G\sqrt\Lambda}.\]
Exact Projection Test
At the independently determined Nariai maximum,
\[q=1,\]
and therefore
\[\Delta S_{c\mid b}=0.\]
Thus the exact physical maximum satisfies the independently proposed R²D marginal condition.
Not Established Here
This addendum does not derive:

• Schwarzschild–de Sitter geometry from primitive R²D counting; • the value of Λ; • the Bekenstein–Hawking calibration; • the microscopic horizon multiplicities; • the Nariai temperature; • the physical clock of the replacement landscape; • or the recurrence relation surviving horizon-branch coalescence.

section: 58. Conclusion
text:
58. Conclusion
Addendum 44 proposed that a gravitational multiplicity well reaches its enclosing limit when the multiplicity distinction separating subordinate and enclosing count boundaries vanishes.
The proposed count coordinate was

\[\Delta S_{E\mid H}=\ln\frac{W_E}{W_H}.\]
Its marginal condition was
\[\Delta S_{E\mid H}=0.\]
That proposal was made without invoking Schwarzschild–de Sitter geometry or the Nariai solution.
Schwarzschild–de Sitter therefore provides an independent exact physical test.
Its black-hole and cosmological horizons are positive roots of
\[f(r)=1-\frac{2GM}{c^2r}-\frac{\Lambda r^2}{3}.\]
The two positive roots are coupled by
\[r_b^2+r_br_c+r_c^2=\frac3\Lambda.\]
Defining
\[q=\frac{r_b}{r_c},\]
their areas are
\[A_b=\frac{12\pi q^2}{\Lambda(1+q+q^2)},\]
and
\[A_c=\frac{12\pi}{\Lambda(1+q+q^2)}.\]
With the common horizon multiplicity calibration,
\[S_b=\ln W_b=\frac{A_b}{4\ell_P^2},\]
and
\[S_c=\ln W_c=\frac{A_c}{4\ell_P^2},\]
the exact multiplicity gap is

\[\Delta S_{c\mid b}=\ln\frac{W_c}{W_b}=\frac{3\pi}{\Lambda\ell_P^2}\frac{1-q^2}{1+q+q^2}.\]
Throughout the ordinary two-horizon regime,
\[q<1,\]
so
\[\Delta S_{c\mid b}>0.\]
The subordinate and enclosing horizon classes remain multiplicatively distinct.
The independently known physical maximum occurs when the two positive roots form a double root:
\[f(r_N)=0,\]
\[f'(r_N)=0.\]
This gives
\[r_N=\frac1{\sqrt\Lambda},\]
and
\[M_N=\frac{c^2}{3G\sqrt\Lambda}.\]
At this exact maximum,
\[r_b=r_c,\]
so
\[q=1.\]
Therefore,
\[A_b=A_c,\]
\[S_b=S_c,\]
and most importantly,
\[\Delta S_{c\mid b}=\ln\frac{W_c}{W_b}=0.\]

The exact maximum-mass gravitational solution therefore reaches precisely the count-level marginal condition proposed independently in Addendum 44.
The enclosing cosmological boundary does not remain fixed while the black-hole multiplicity well grows.
Instead,
\[A_b\uparrow\]
while
\[A_c\downarrow.\]
At zero black-hole mass,
\[A_{\mathrm{dS}}=\frac{12\pi}{\Lambda}.\]
At Nariai,
\[A_b=A_c=\frac{4\pi}{\Lambda}.\]
Thus the enclosing area contracts to one third of its pure de Sitter value while the subordinate horizon grows to meet it.
The limit is therefore not a local well filling a fixed box.
It is coupled boundary reorganization.
At the point where the multiplicity gap disappears, the two positive horizon roots also coalesce.
The old two-horizon count classification has lost the distinction required to sustain it.
The physical system need not disappear.
A replacement gravitational landscape can remain.
What fails is the old classification.
The clock and recurrence associated with that replacement landscape are separate questions.
They come next.
The causal hierarchy established here is
shared gravitational relation → coupled horizon multiplicities → multiplicity-gap closure → areal equality → root… [PDF line clipped; author review required.]

Thus:

multiplicity-gap closure occurs before the Nariai limit.

And more specifically:
the Nariai maximum mass is the physical source-coordinate read of an exact gravitational boundary… [PDF line clipped; author review required.]

title: Addendum 46 — Boundary-Clock Replacement Occurs Before Nariai Temperature
section: Abstract
text:
Abstract
Addendum 45 established that the Schwarzschild–de Sitter black-hole and cosmological horizon multiplicity classes lose their distinction at the Nariai limit.
Their multiplicity gap,
\[\Delta S_{c\mid b}=S_c-S_b=\ln\frac{W_c}{W_b},\]
satisfies
\[\Delta S_{c\mid b}>0\]
throughout the ordinary two-horizon regime and approaches
\[\Delta S_{c\mid b}\longrightarrow0\]
when
\[r_b\longrightarrow r_c.\]
At that same physical boundary, the ordinary Schwarzschild–de Sitter horizon surface gravities vanish:
\[\kappa_b^{(0)}\longrightarrow0,\qquad\kappa_c^{(0)}\longrightarrow0.\]
Consequently the corresponding static-patch phase-frequency reads,
\[\omega_h^{(0)}=\frac{\kappa_h^{(0)}}{2\pi c},\]
also vanish.
Read without regard to boundary ownership, this might appear to imply that recurrence itself stops at Nariai.
R²D does not permit that inference.

A physical clock is a calibrated read belonging to a specified count boundary. When the distinction defining that boundary disappears, the physical clock belonging to that classification may itself become degenerate.
Schwarzschild–de Sitter provides an exact example.
The ordinary two-horizon static clock is normalized relative to a reference relation that also degenerates as the two horizon branches coalesce.
Let
\[r_g\]
denote the geodesic static reference radius satisfying
\[f'(r_g)=0.\]
Define the corresponding static normalization factor
\[N_{\mathrm{stat}}\equiv\sqrt{f(r_g)}.\]
As Nariai is approached,
\[N_{\mathrm{stat}}\longrightarrow0.\]
More strongly, with
\[q=\frac{r_b}{r_c}\]
and
\[\epsilon\equiv1-q,\]
the multiplicity gap, both ordinary surface gravities, and the clock normalization all vanish linearly:
\[\Delta S_{c\mid b}=O(\epsilon),\]
\[\kappa_b^{(0)}=O(\epsilon),\]
\[\kappa_c^{(0)}=O(\epsilon),\]
and
\[N_{\mathrm{stat}}=O(\epsilon).\]
The zero of the old clock therefore occurs at the same boundary at which the count distinction defining the old two-horizon landscape disappears.

But the ratio
\[\frac{\kappa_h^{(0)}}{N_{\mathrm{stat}}}\]
has a finite limiting value.
Under the Bousso–Hawking normalization,
\[\kappa_h^{\mathrm{BH}}=\frac{\kappa_h^{(0)}}{N_{\mathrm{stat}}},\]
and at Nariai,
\[\kappa_N=c^2\sqrt{\Lambda}.\]
The corresponding phase-frequency read is
\[\omega_N=\frac{c\sqrt\Lambda}{2\pi}.\]
Only afterward does thermal dimensionalization give
\[k_BT_N=\hbar\omega_N=\frac{\hbar c\sqrt\Lambda}{2\pi}.\]
The finite quantity \(\omega_N\) should not be interpreted as the old static-patch clock recovering from zero.
The old clock satisfies
\[\omega_b^{(0)},\omega_c^{(0)}\longrightarrow0.\]
The finite quantity
\[\omega_N\]
belongs to the replacement Nariai landscape.
The old and new clock reads have different boundary owners.
Thus the correct R²D order is

two-horizon count distinction


\(\Downarrow\)


two-horizon clock calibration



\(\Downarrow\)

\[\Delta S_{c\mid b}\longrightarrow0\]

\(\Downarrow\)

\[\kappa_b^{(0)},\kappa_c^{(0)},N_{\mathrm{stat}}\longrightarrow0\]

\(\Downarrow\)


old clock classification becomes degenerate


\(\Downarrow\)


Nariai replacement landscape


\(\Downarrow\)

\[\omega_N=\frac{c\sqrt\Lambda}{2\pi}\]

\(\Downarrow\)

\[T_N.\]
Temperature comes last.
Therefore:

boundary-clock replacement occurs before Nariai temperature.

More precisely:
the vanishing Schwarzschild–de Sitter static-patch temperature is the degeneration of a boundary-s

\[r_g^3=\frac12r_br_c(r_b+r_c).\]

Using
\[q\equiv\frac{r_b}{r_c},\]
we obtain
\[r_g=r_c\left[\frac{q(1+q)}2\right]^{1/3}.\]
The clock reference therefore changes as the two horizon branches reorganize.
It is not a fixed external observer independent of the gravitational landscape.

we have
\[\frac{2GM}{c^2r_g}=\frac{2\Lambda r_g^2}{3}.\]
Hence,
\[f(r_g)=1-\Lambda r_g^2.\]
Therefore,
\[N_{\mathrm{stat}}^2=1-\Lambda r_g^2.\]

text:
51. Logical Status
Established in Addendum 45
The Schwarzschild–de Sitter multiplicity gap satisfies
\[\Delta S_{c\mid b}>0\]
throughout the ordinary two-horizon regime and
\[\Delta S_{c\mid b}\longrightarrow0\]
at Nariai.

The old two-horizon count classification becomes marginal.
Conventional Schwarzschild–de Sitter Input
The ordinary horizon surface gravities are
\[\kappa_b^{(0)}=\frac{c^2}{2}\left(\frac1{r_b}-\Lambda r_b\right),\]
and
\[\kappa_c^{(0)}=\frac{c^2}{2}\left(\Lambda r_c-\frac1{r_c}\right).\]
They vanish as
\[r_b\longrightarrow r_c.\]
Conventional Reference Normalization
The geodesic static reference satisfies
\[f'(r_g)=0,\]
and the corresponding clock normalization is
\[N_{\mathrm{stat}}=\sqrt{f(r_g)}.\]
At Nariai,
\[N_{\mathrm{stat}}\longrightarrow0.\]
Derived Near-Nariai Scaling
For
\[\begin{aligned}\epsilon&=1-q,\\N_{\mathrm{stat}}&=\epsilon/2+O(\epsilon^2),\\\kappa_b^{(0)}&=(c^2\sqrt\Lambda/2)\epsilon+O(\epsilon^2),\\\kappa_c^{(0)}&=(c^2\sqrt\Lambda/2)\epsilon+O(\epsilon^2).\end{aligned}\]
and

\[\Delta S_{c\mid b}=\frac{2\pi}{\Lambda\ell_P^2}\epsilon+O(\epsilon^2).\]
Conventional Bousso–Hawking Limit
With
\[\kappa_h^{\mathrm{BH}}=\frac{\kappa_h^{(0)}}{N_{\mathrm{stat}}},\]
the Nariai limit is
\[\kappa_N=c^2\sqrt{\Lambda}.\]
Therefore,
\[\omega_N=\frac{c\sqrt\Lambda}{2\pi}.\]
And under thermal dimensionalization,
\[k_BT_N=\frac{\hbar c\sqrt\Lambda}{2\pi}.\]
New R²D Interpretation
The ordinary zero-frequency limit is interpreted as degeneration of the physical clock belonging to the disappearing two-horizon classification.
The finite normalized Nariai frequency is interpreted as a physical clock read belonging to the replacement landscape.
Not Established Here
This addendum does not establish:

• that \(\omega_N\) is primitive R²D recurrence; • that Bousso–Hawking normalization is the uniquely fundamental temperature prescription for every Schwarzschild–de Sitter state; • that primitive recurrence has been proven to persist across the transition; • that the old and new clocks are the same physical coordinate; • that the Nariai geometry is derived from primitive R²D counting; • or what invariant count relation, if any, survives the boundary replacement.

Those questions remain separate.

section: 53. Conclusion
text:
53. Conclusion
The Nariai limit does not merely merge two horizon areas.
It also destroys the physical clock normalization belonging to the ordinary Schwarzschild–de Sitter two- horizon static patch.
Addendum 45 established that the multiplicity distinction between the black-hole and cosmological horizons vanishes:
\[\Delta S_{c\mid b}=\ln\frac{W_c}{W_b}\longrightarrow0.\]
At precisely the same boundary,
\[\kappa_b^{(0)},\kappa_c^{(0)}\longrightarrow0.\]
Thus the ordinary phase-frequency reads satisfy
\[\omega_b^{(0)},\omega_c^{(0)}\longrightarrow0.\]
But the reference defining that old static clock also degenerates.
For the geodesic static reference,
\[N_{\mathrm{stat}}=\sqrt{f(r_g)}\longrightarrow0.\]
Near Nariai, with
\[\epsilon=1-\frac{r_b}{r_c},\]
the four relations

\[\Delta S_{c\mid b},\]
\[\kappa_b^{(0)},\]
\[\kappa_c^{(0)},\]
and
\[N_{\mathrm{stat}}\]
all vanish linearly in
\[\epsilon.\]
The old horizon distinction and its old physical clock therefore become degenerate together.
The correct limiting object is not the numerator alone.
It is the boundary-normalized ratio
\[\frac{\kappa_h^{(0)}}{N_{\mathrm{stat}}}.\]
Its finite limit is
\[\kappa_N=c^2\sqrt{\Lambda}.\]
Therefore the replacement Nariai landscape possesses the finite phase-frequency read
\[\omega_N=\frac{c\sqrt\Lambda}{2\pi}.\]
This does not mean the old clock survives unchanged.
The old clock goes to zero.
The replacement boundary possesses a different clock calibration.
Only afterward does thermal dimensionalization produce
\[T_N=\frac{\hbar c\sqrt\Lambda}{2\pi k_B}.\]
The zero of the old static-patch temperature therefore cannot, by itself, establish disappearance of all recurrence.
It establishes the disappearance of a specified boundary-owned clock.

The physical lesson is the same one that R²D has repeatedly exposed elsewhere:
a projected coordinate can vanish because the boundary defining its calibration is vanishing with it.
The clock does not define the boundary.
The boundary defines the clock.
When the boundary classification changes, the clock may change with it.

Abstract
Addendum 46 established that the Nariai limit is a boundary-clock replacement problem.

\[\Delta S_{c\mid b}=\ln\frac{W_c}{W_b}\longrightarrow0,\]

\[\omega_b^{(0)},\omega_c^{(0)}\longrightarrow0.\]
The normalization defining that clock vanishes at the same boundary,
\[N_{\mathrm{stat}}\longrightarrow0.\]
The replacement Nariai landscape nevertheless possesses the finite boundary-appropriate phase-frequency read
\[\omega_N=\frac{c\sqrt\Lambda}{2\pi}.\]
Thus neither the old clock nor the old two-horizon multiplicity classification survives unchanged.
The present addendum asks the next R²D question:

If the physical count and physical clock both change under boundary replacement, does a deeper relation remain coherent?

\[r_N=\frac1{\sqrt\Lambda},\]
\[S_N=\frac\pi{\Lambda\ell_P^2},\]

Therefore,

Then both horizon calibrations satisfy

\[4\pi\alpha_G^\omega S=1.\]
This relation is not introduced here as a new primitive R²D law.
It follows algebraically whenever two physical calibrations hold:
\[S=\frac{\pi r^2}{\ell_P^2},\]
and
\[\omega=\frac{c}{2\pi r}.\]
Its significance is instead relational.
Pure de Sitter and Nariai possess different radii, different horizon multiplicities, different physical clocks, and different boundary classifications. Yet both realize the same dimensionless count–clock calibration.
Thus boundary replacement need not preserve either physical coordinate separately.
It can preserve the relation connecting them.
This is the R²D meaning of replacement coherence:

state identity changes; relational organization persists.

The result is not a conservation law along the full Schwarzschild–de Sitter family.
It does not imply
\[\frac{d}{dM}(S\omega^2)=0.\]
Nor does it imply that pure de Sitter is the state immediately preceding Nariai.
Instead, the result identifies a common gravitational calibration class realized by two different horizon landscapes.
Therefore:

horizon count–clock calibration persists across boundary replacement.

boundary replacement can change both the physical horizon count and the physical clock while pres… [PDF line clipped; author review required.]

Multiply by

\[B_{\mathrm{dS}}=B_N.\]

title: Addendum 48 — Coupled Horizon Retention Occurs Before Kerr–Newman Geometry
section: Abstract
text:
Abstract
Schwarzschild geometry contains a horizon boundary whose exterior-directed gravitational read reaches complete retention.
Kerr, Reissner–Nordström, and Kerr–Newman introduce additional structure.
At fixed physical mass, the horizon can occupy different rotational and charge states. Conventional gravity represents these states using angular momentum
\[J\]
and charge
\[Q\]
and their changes enter the black-hole first law through the work terms
\[\Omega_H dJ\]
and
\[\Phi_H dQ\]
Recursively Realized Distinguishability (R²D) asks what count architecture exists before those physical work terms are interpreted geometrically.
Define the mass-owned dimensionless scale
\[j_M\equiv\frac{GM^2}{\hbar c}\]
Define the rotational macrostate coordinate
\[j\equiv\frac J\hbar\]
and the dimensionless charge coordinate

\[q\equiv\frac Q{q_P},\qquad q_P=\sqrt{4\pi\epsilon_0\hbar c}\]
The Kerr–Newman horizon condition becomes
\[j^2+j_Mq^2\le j_M^2\]
Thus rotation and charge are not two unrelated additions to a Schwarzschild horizon.
They are two distinguishable physical macrostate coordinates within one fixed-mass admissible horizon domain.
Define
\[\Delta_{\mathrm{KN}}=\sqrt{j_M^2-j^2-j_Mq^2}\]
Then the phase-normalized horizon roots are
\[x_\pm=j_M\pm\Delta_{\mathrm{KN}}.\]
The outer-horizon Bekenstein–Hawking multiplicity coordinate is
\[S_+ (j, q) = \ln W_+ = 2\pi (j_M + \Delta_{\mathrm{KN}} ) - \pi q^2\]
This is the native logarithmic multiplicity landscape of the physically calibrated stationary horizon boundary.
The Kerr–Newman first law is
\[d(M c^2 ) = k_B T_H dS_+ + \Omega_H dJ + \Phi_H dQ\]
Along the fixed-mass stationary family,
\[d(M c^2 ) = 0\]
Therefore,
\[k_B T_H dS_+ = - (\Omega_H dJ + \Phi_H dQ)\]
Define the physical dimensionless retention differential
\[dR_{\mathrm{KN}}=\frac{\Omega_H\,dJ+\Phi_H\,dQ}{k_BT_H}\]
Then
\[dR_{\mathrm{KN}}=-dS_+.\]

Because S+ is a state function, the total coupled retention one-form is exact.
The two conventional work channels may be written
\[dR_J=\frac{\Omega_H\,dJ}{k_BT_H}\]
and
\[dR_Q=\frac{\Phi_H\,dQ}{k_BT_H}\]
But on the full two-dimensional Kerr–Newman macrostate domain, these channel contributions are not separately exact in general.
Their sum is:
\[dR_{\mathrm{KN}} = dR_J + dR_Q = -dS_+\]
The integrable object therefore belongs to the coupled horizon boundary, not independently to rotation and charge.
Under the R²D stationary-state mapping, enclosing possibility changes in the same differential relation:
\[dP_{\mathrm{KN}} = dR_{\mathrm{KN}}\]
Hence,
\[dA_{\mathrm{KN}}=dP_{\mathrm{KN}}-dR_{\mathrm{KN}}=0.\]
This is a differential stall condition over the stationary Kerr–Newman macrostate manifold.
It must not be confused with an absolute statement
\[P_{\mathrm{KN}} = R_{\mathrm{KN}}\]
which requires an independently specified integration constant.
Nor should it be confused with extremality.
Differential stall holds throughout the stationary family under this mapping.
Extremality occurs only when
\[\Delta_{\mathrm{KN}} = 0\]
Using the canonical R²D possibility relation

\[P=\ln\frac\Theta W=\ln\Theta-S\]
we have
\[dP = d \ln \Theta - dS\]
Since
\[dP_{\mathrm{KN}} = dR_{\mathrm{KN}} = -dS_+\]
it follows that
\[d \ln \Theta_{\mathrm{KN}} = 0\]
Thus the enclosing compatible multiplicity remains invariant across the connected fixed-mass stationary macrostate family.
Rotation and charge redistribute the realized horizon multiplicity landscape without changing the enclosing compatible count under this stationary-stall mapping.
Relative to the same-mass Schwarzschild state,
\[S_{\mathrm{Schw}} = 4\pi j_M\]
Define the cumulative physical retention read
\[R_{\mathrm{KN}} \equiv S_{\mathrm{Schw}} - S_+\]
Then
\[S_+ + R_{\mathrm{KN}} = S_{\mathrm{Schw}}\]
This is a physical state-space identity.
It does not identify
\[S_{\mathrm{Schw}}\]
with primitive possibility or with
\[\ln \Theta\]
The inner horizon supplies a useful but secondary geometric comparison.
Its multiplicity coordinate is
\[S_- = 2\pi (j_M - \Delta_{\mathrm{KN}} ) - \pi q^2\]

The cumulative retention read is
\[R_{\mathrm{KN}} = 2\pi (j_M - \Delta_{\mathrm{KN}} ) + \pi q^2\]
Therefore,
\[R_{\mathrm{KN}} = S_- + 2\pi q^2\]
Only on the pure Kerr axis,
\[q = 0\]
does this reduce to
\[R_J = S_-\]
Thus the Kerr inner-horizon equality is not a universal R²D identification.
Reissner–Nordström and the full Kerr–Newman family show that the inner horizon is not the primitive retention coordinate.
The correct hierarchy is therefore

fixed-mass horizon boundary


↓


(j, q) admissible macrostate domain


↓

\[S_+ (j, q) = \ln W_+\]

↓

\[dR_{\mathrm{KN}}=\frac{\Omega_H\,dJ+\Phi_H\,dQ}{k_BT_H}=-dS_+\]

↓

under the stationary-state R²D mapping,
\[dP_{\mathrm{KN}} = dR_{\mathrm{KN}}\]

↓

\[dA_{\mathrm{KN}} = 0\]

↓


\[d \ln \Theta_{\mathrm{KN}} = 0\]

↓


Kerr–Newman geometry.

Thus:

coupled horizon retention occurs before Kerr–Newman geometry.

More specifically:
rotation and charge are distinct physical work projections of one integrable retention relation owned

can have equal gravitational horizon multiplicity while remaining physically distinct charge states.
Thus:

orientation distinction \(\\ne\) multiplicity diff

The boundary can own both.

17. The First Law Supplies the Physical Work Reads
The Kerr–Newman first law may be written
\[d(M c^2 ) = k_B T_H dS_+ + \Omega_H dJ + \Phi_H dQ\]
Here
\[\Omega_H\]
is the horizon angular velocity and
\[\Phi_H\]
the horizon electrostatic potential.
The two conventional productive work reads are therefore
\[\Omega_H dJ\]
and

\[\Phi_H dQ\]

section: 18. Restrict to the Fixed-Mass Stationary Family
text:
18. Restrict to the Fixed-Mass Stationary Family
For the macrostate family considered here,
\[dM = 0\]
Hence,
\[d(M c^2 ) = 0\]
The first law becomes
\[k_B T_H dS_+ + \Omega_H dJ + \Phi_H dQ = 0\]
Therefore,
\[\frac{\Omega_H\,dJ+\Phi_H\,dQ}{k_BT_H}=-dS_+\]

text:
19. Define the Coupled Physical Retention Read
Map the dimensionless productive work coordinate to R²D retention:
\[dR_{\mathrm{KN}}=\frac{\Omega_H\,dJ+\Phi_H\,dQ}{k_BT_H}\]
Then
\[dR_{\mathrm{KN}}=-dS_+.\]
This relation is exact over the connected stationary macrostate domain.

text:
20. Retention Is Not Angular Momentum or Charge
The mapping does not identify
\[J = R\]
or
\[Q = R\]

Nor does it identify either work term alone with a primitive independent retention variable.
Instead,
\[R_{\mathrm{KN}}\]
belongs to the transition relation of the full coupled boundary.
The physical coordinates J and Q describe how that relation is read.
