title: Addendum 61 — Peer Energy and Boundary Support Occur Before Cosmological Energy
section: 72. Conclusion
text:
72. Conclusion
Cosmological energy density appears so naturally in the Friedmann equation that it is easy to treat
\[\epsilon_\zeta\]
as a primitive description of how much material content the universe contains.
R²D requires an earlier decomposition.
The cosmological boundary first contains recursively realized peers.
Those peers possess a compatible joint state before mass or energy has been assigned to them.
A physical source projection can then assign that peer organization an energy coordinate
\[ E\zeta,i\]
In the simplest pressureless limit, peer coupling acquires mass through
\[ m_\alpha=M_{\mathrm{cal}}\mu_\alpha.\],
and the comoving source energy becomes
\[ E_\zeta^{\mathrm{dust}}=M_{\mathrm{cal}}c^2\sum_\alpha\mu_\alpha\]
More generally, the mature source read includes energy, momentum, pressure, stress, and flux.
Independently, the enclosing cosmological boundary acquires a geometric read.
Area comes first:
\[ A_{\zeta,i}\]
For a fixed isotropic comoving support domain, volume follows as
\[ V_{\zeta,i}=\eta_{k,\chi}A_{\zeta,i}^{3/2}\]
Only then can the physical source-density coordinate be constructed:
\[\epsilon_{\zeta,i}=\frac{E_{\zeta,i}}{V_{\zeta,i}}\]
The Friedmann matter-energy term is therefore

\[ F_\epsilon=\frac{8\pi G}{3c^2}\frac{E_\zeta}{V_\zeta}\]
Or, using gravitational energy place value,
\[ F_\epsilon=\frac{8\pi c^2\ell_{E,\zeta}}{3V_\zeta}\]
The conventional statement that energy density gravitates is therefore a mature physical compression of two prior projections:

peer energy

and

boundary support.

Density does not create either one.
It is their ratio.
This also changes the meaning of cosmological dilution.
For pressureless conserved source energy,
\[\epsilon_\zeta^{\mathrm{dust}}\propto a^{-3}\]
does not mean primitive peer structure is disappearing.
The physical source read remains fixed while its projected support grows.
For sources with pressure, the numerator changes with the support according to the physical work relation, yielding the standard continuity equation.
None of these physical relations requires identifying pressure with R²D possibility, energy density with retention, or matter with primitive count.
The causal ordering remains:

peer-boundary organization


↓


physical source energy

combined with


physical boundary support

to produce

energy density

and only afterward

Friedmann source contribution.

The central statement is therefore:
cosmological energy density is not a primitive amount of substance distributed through pre-existing
And hence:
 peer energy and boundary support occur before cosmological energy density.

title: Addendum 62 — Boundary Geometry Occurs Before the Friedmann Curvature Term
section: Abstract
text:
Abstract
Addendum 60 showed that the Friedmann equation partitions one already-defined physical rate magnitude,
\[ H^2\]
into several downstream gravitational coordinates.
Addendum 61 then deprojected the matter-energy contribution,
\[\frac{8\pi G}{3c^2}\epsilon_\zeta\]
into two prior physical reads:

peer-energy read

and

boundary-support read.

The next Friedmann contribution is
\[ F_k=-\frac{kc^2}{a^2}\]
This term has fundamentally different physical ownership.
It is not a source-density term.
For normalized FLRW spatial geometry,
\[ k\in\{-1,0,+1\}.\]
labels the constant-curvature projection class, whereas
\[ K_\zeta\equiv\frac{k}{a^2}\]

is the state-dependent physical sectional curvature of the spatial geometry.
Equivalently, the intrinsic scalar curvature of a constant-cosmological-time spatial slice is
\[{}^{(3)}R_\zeta=\frac{6k}{a^2}=6K_\zeta\]
Thus the Friedmann curvature contribution can be written
\[ F_k=-c^2K_\zeta.\]
or
\[ F_k=-\frac{c^2}{6}\,{}^{(3)}R_\zeta\]
The curvature term is therefore already a physical geometric read.
Addendum 56 established that, for a fixed comoving shell χ,
\[ A_\zeta=4\pi a^2S_k^2(\chi).\]
Solving for the scale factor gives
\[ a^2=\frac{A_\zeta}{4\pi S_k^2(\chi)}\]
Therefore,
\[ K_\zeta=\frac{k}{a^2}=\frac{4\pi k S_k^2(\chi)}{A_\zeta}\]
The spatial scalar curvature is correspondingly
\[{}^{(3)}R_\zeta=\frac{24\pi kS_k^2(\chi)}{A_\zeta}\]
And the Friedmann curvature contribution becomes
\[ F_k=-\frac{4\pi kc^2 S_k^2(\chi)}{A_\zeta}\]
Once the curvature class and comoving comparison domain are fixed, physical spatial curvature therefore scales as the inverse of cosmological boundary area:

\[ K_\zeta\propto A_\zeta^{-1}\]
The geometric ordering is consequently
\[ B_\zeta\to A_\zeta\to K_\zeta\to F_k\]
The normalized label k does not supply physical curvature magnitude by itself.
Instead,
\(k\) = geometric projection class
and
\(A_\zeta\) = state-dependent geometric place value
jointly determine
\(K_\zeta\) = physical spatial curvature
This also explains why cosmological expansion changes the magnitude of curvature without changing the FLRW curvature class.
For fixed nonzero k ,
\[ K_\zeta\propto A_\zeta^{-1}\]
Hence,
\[ d\ln|K_\zeta|=-d\ln A_\zeta\]
Using
\[ H=\frac12\frac{d\ln A_\zeta}{dt}\]
we obtain
\[\frac{\dot K_\zeta}{K_\zeta}=-2H\]
and therefore
\[\dot K_\zeta=-2HK_\zeta.\]
Likewise,

\[\dot{{}^{(3)}R}_\zeta=-2H\,{}^{(3)}R_\zeta\]
The curvature class does not evolve:
\[ k=\mathrm{constant}.\]
while its physical magnitude does.
The distinction is crucial for R²D.
The primitive cosmological state is defined through compatible peer-boundary realization before FLRW geometry is assigned.
The curvature class k therefore cannot be identified by definition with R²D constraint, retention, possibility, or asymmetry.
In particular,
\[ k\ne C_\zeta\]
and
\[ K_\zeta\ne R_\zeta\]
Any such relation would require an independent bridge from peer-compatibility structure to the physical curvature class.
The present addendum does not yet derive why a particular R²D cosmological realization projects as
\[ k=+1,\quad k=0,\quad\text{or}\quad k=-1\]
It derives the later relation:

Once an isotropic constant-curvature projection class is selected, the magnitude of its physical curvature is determined by the cosmological boundary-area read.

This separates curvature from matter-energy.
For pressureless conserved source energy, Addendum 61 gave
\[ F_{\mathrm{dust}}\propto A_\zeta^{-3/2}\]
By contrast,
\[ F_k\propto A_\zeta^{-1}\]

The different scalings follow because the terms have different physical ownership.
Matter-energy is a source-energy read divided by a three-dimensional support volume:
\[ V_\zeta\propto A_\zeta^{3/2}\]
Curvature is an inverse squared-length property of the projected boundary geometry:
\[ K_\zeta\propto A_\zeta^{-1}\]
The Friedmann equation can therefore be written, in the pressureless-source limit, almost entirely in area coordinates:
\[ H^2=\frac{8\pi c^2\ell_{E,\zeta}}{3\eta_{k,\chi}A_\zeta^{3/2}}-\frac{4\pi kc^2S_k^2(\chi)}{A_\zeta}+\frac{\Lambda c^2}{3}\]
The three contributions now reveal three different area-scaling classes:
\[ F_{\mathrm{dust}}\propto A_\zeta^{-3/2}\]
\[ F_k\propto A_\zeta^{-1}\]
and
\[ F_\Lambda\propto A_\zeta^0\]
The conventional scale-factor forms,
\(a^{-3}\), \(a^{-2}\), and \(a^0\), respectively.
are therefore later expressions of different physical boundary reads.
The central statement is:
the Friedmann curvature term is not a primitive negative source contribution. It is the rate-squared
And hence:

Boundary geometry occurs before the Friedmann curvature term.

58. Conclusion
The curvature term in the Friedmann equation,
\[-\frac{kc^2}{a^2}\]

Its physical origin is different.
The normalized parameter
\[ k\]

\[ A_\zeta=4\pi a^2S_k^2(\chi).\]

\[ K_{\zeta,i}=\frac{4\pi kS_k^2(\chi)}{A_{\zeta,i}}\]
The Friedmann curvature contribution is consequently

\[ F_k=-\frac{4\pi kc^2 S_k^2(\chi)}{A_\zeta}\]
Physical curvature is therefore an inverse-area read of the projected cosmological boundary.
As the boundary area grows,
\[|K_\zeta|\propto A_\zeta^{-1}\]
decreases.

This differs fundamentally from the matter-energy contribution.
Matter-energy depends on source energy divided by three-dimensional boundary support and therefore scales, for conserved dust energy, as
\[ A_\zeta^{-3/2}\]

\[ A_\zeta^{-1}\]
The difference in Friedmann scaling is therefore not merely a difference in algebraic exponent.
It reflects a difference in physical ownership.
The matter term is a source/support read.
The curvature term is a geometric read.
Rewriting curvature as an effective density does not erase that distinction.
Within R²D, the unresolved primitive question lies one level earlier:

What property of compatible cosmological peer organization selects the constant-curvature / projection class k ?

That question remains open.
But once the class has been selected, its physical magnitude and its Friedmann contribution follow from the boundary-area projection.
The central statement is therefore:

the Friedmann curvature term is not a primitive negative source contribution. It is the rate-squared
And hence:

Boundary geometry occurs before the Friedmann curvature term.

title: Addendum 63 — Fixed Reference Area Occurs Before Dark-Energy Attribution
section: Abstract
text:
Abstract

Addenda 61 and 62 deprojected the first two terms of the Friedmann rate constraint.
The matter-energy contribution,
\[ \frac{8\pi G}{3c^2}\varepsilon_\zeta, \]
was shown to depend on the physical energy read of cosmological peer organization divided by the physical support volume of the enclosing boundary.
For conserved pressureless source energy,
\[ F_{\mathrm{dust}}\propto A_\zeta^{-3/2}. \]
The spatial-curvature contribution,
\[ -\frac{k c^2}{a^2}, \]
was shown to be a geometric read of the evolving cosmological boundary.
For fixed curvature class,
\[ F_k\propto A_\zeta^{-1}. \]
The remaining Friedmann contribution is
\[ F_\Lambda=\frac{\Lambda c^2}{3}. \]
For constant Λ, this term has no dependence on the evolving cosmological boundary area:
\[ F_\Lambda\propto A_\zeta^0. \]
It therefore has different physical ownership from both matter-energy and spatial curvature.

For positive Λ, define the geometric length scale
\[ L_\Lambda\equiv\sqrt{\frac{3}{\Lambda}}. \]
Then
\[ F_\Lambda=\frac{c^2}{L_\Lambda^2}. \]
Associate with this length the reference area
\[ A_\Lambda\equiv4\pi L_\Lambda^2=\frac{12\pi}{\Lambda}. \]
Therefore,
\[ F_\Lambda=\frac{4\pi c^2}{A_\Lambda}. \]
The cosmological-constant contribution is thus an inverse-area geometric read.
But the relevant area is not the evolving cosmological macrostate area
\[ A_\zeta\]
It is the fixed reference area
\[ A_\Lambda\]
Thus:
\[ A_\Lambda\ne A_\zeta\]
The distinction is already visible in exact de Sitter geometry.
In the pure-Λ, spatially flat limit,
\[\epsilon=0,\quad k=0\]
the Friedmann constraint becomes
\[ H^2=\frac{\Lambda c^2}{3}=\frac{c^2}{L_\Lambda^2}\]
Define

Λ c
\[ H_\Lambda\equiv c\sqrt{\frac{\Lambda}{3}}=\frac{c}{L_\Lambda}\]
Then
\[ H^2=H_\Lambda^2\]
The first-order geometric evolution still possesses two branches:
\[ H=\pm H_\Lambda. \]
Correspondingly,
\[ a(t)=a_0e^{\pm H_\Lambda t}. \]
For a fixed comoving boundary,
\[ A_\zeta(t)\propto a^2(t), \]
so
\[ A_\zeta(t)\propto e^{\pm2H_\Lambda t}\]
The evolving cosmological area therefore changes while
\[ A_\Lambda=\frac{12\pi}{\Lambda} \]
remains constant.
Thus:
\[\Delta A_\zeta\ne0\]
while
\[\Delta A_\Lambda=0\]
The cosmological state evolves relative to a fixed geometric reference scale.
This also clarifies the causal status of Λ.
Positive Λ fixes a rate magnitude,
\[ H_\Lambda^2\]

but does not determine the sign of H .
Therefore,
\[\Lambda\ne A_\zeta\]
and
\[\Lambda\ne\Xi_\star\]
A state-independent positive cosmological constant does not supply the primitive cosmological arrow.
It contributes to the allowable magnitude of the gravitational rate after the directional branch has already been selected.
The same distinction remains in the acceleration equation.
For pure de Sitter geometry,
\[\frac{\ddot a}{a}=\frac{\Lambda c^2}{3}=H_\Lambda^2\]
Both
\[ a(t)=a_0e^{H_\Lambda t}\]
and
\[ a(t)=a_0e^{-H_\Lambda t}\]
satisfy
\[\frac{\ddot a}{a}=H_\Lambda^2\]
Thus positive geometric acceleration does not by itself specify expansion rather than contraction.
The directional information remains upstream.
Only after the geometric contribution has been defined may the same term be rewritten as an effective source density.
Define
\[\epsilon_\Lambda=\frac{\Lambda c^4}{8\pi G}\]
Then

8πG
\[ F_\Lambda=\frac{8\pi G}{3c^2}\epsilon_\Lambda\]
If this effective component is represented as a separately conserved homogeneous perfect-fluid source, then
\[\dot\epsilon_\Lambda=0\]
The physical continuity equation,
\[\dot\epsilon_\Lambda+3H(\epsilon_\Lambda+p_\Lambda)=0\]
therefore gives, for nonzero H ,
\[ p_\Lambda=-\epsilon_\Lambda\]
Hence:
\[ w_\Lambda\equiv\frac{p_\Lambda}{\epsilon_\Lambda}=-1\]
The w = −1 vacuum-energy representation is therefore an equivalent source-coordinate representation of the fixed Λ contribution.
It does not establish that a primitive vacuum substance precedes the geometric relation.
Earlier gravitational addenda reached the same logical distinction from de Sitter horizon physics. Exact de Sitter permits Λ to be rewritten through a horizon recurrence/ruler calibration, but that result was explicitly not taken to mean that Λ is primitive recurrence, dark energy, or R2D background.
Likewise, the pure de Sitter horizon area was previously identified as a reference area rather than an invariant enclosing capacity when additional gravitational structure is present.
The same distinction now enters the cosmological Friedmann reconstruction.
The area
\[ A_\Lambda\]
sets a fixed physical reference scale of the gravitational projection.
It does not define the changing cosmological boundary.
Nor does its associated horizon recurrence define the terminal R2D clock. The earlier de Sitter analysis explicitly distinguished horizon/background recurrence from both the master directed recurrence and the missing recurrence of the open cosmological turbine.
The central statement is therefore:


Central statement. The cosmological-constant term is not initially a primitive source density or a primitive cosmological arrow. It is a state-independent rate-squared contribution set by a fixed geometric reference scale. For positive \(\Lambda\), that scale can be written as the pure de Sitter reference area \(A_\Lambda\). Only afterward can the same contribution be represented as an \(\epsilon_\Lambda\) vacuum-energy density and attributed phenomenologically to dark energy. Fixed reference area occurs before dark-energy attribution.

The same contribution may then be rewritten as a source coordinate:
\[ F_\Lambda=\frac{8\pi G}{3c^2}\epsilon_\Lambda\]

Only at this later physical level does the conventional vacuum-energy or dark-energy attribution enter.

fixed gravitational reference scale

equivalent w = −1 source representation

dark-energy attribution.

title: Addendum 63 — Fixed Reference Area Occurs Before Dark-Energy Attribution
section: 66. Conclusion
text:
66. Conclusion
The cosmological-constant term is the only contribution to the standard Friedmann partition that does not dilute with the evolving cosmological boundary area.
Matter-energy changes because source energy is compared with changing physical support.
Spatial curvature changes because a fixed curvature class is compared with changing geometric area.
A constant Λ does neither.

Instead,
\[ F_\Lambda=\frac{\Lambda c^2}{3}\]
defines a fixed rate-squared scale.
For positive Λ, this scale can be written geometrically as
\[ L_\Lambda=\sqrt{\frac{3}{\Lambda}}\]
and
\[ A_\Lambda=\frac{12\pi}{\Lambda}\]
Thus:
\[ F_\Lambda=\frac{4\pi c^2}{A_\Lambda}\]
This reference area is not the evolving cosmological boundary area.
In exact de Sitter geometry,
\[ A_\zeta(t)\propto e^{\pm2H_\Lambda t}\]
while
\[ A_\Lambda\]
remains fixed.
Nor does Λ determine cosmological direction.
The same positive constant satisfies
\[ H=\pm H_\Lambda\]
It fixes the magnitude of the de Sitter rate but not the orientation of cosmological realization.
That directional datum remains upstream in the R2D causal architecture.
The same fixed geometric contribution can subsequently be written as

Λc4
\[\epsilon_\Lambda=\frac{\Lambda c^4}{8\pi G}\]
with
\[ p_\Lambda=-\epsilon_\Lambda\]
This produces the familiar
\[ w_\Lambda\equiv\frac{p_\Lambda}{\epsilon_\Lambda}=-1\]
vacuum-energy representation.
But the representation comes later.
It does not establish that vacuum energy is the primitive cause of the relation, nor that Λ is R2D possibility, background, asymmetry, or terminal nonclosure.
After Addenda 61–63, the three sectors of the first Friedmann equation can therefore be written as three physically distinct boundary reads:
\[ F_{\mathrm{matter}}\sim\frac{\text{peer-energy place value}}{A_\zeta^{3/2}}\]
\[ F_k\sim\frac{\text{curvature class}}{A_\zeta}\]
and
\[ F_\Lambda\sim\frac1{A_\Lambda}\]
The first belongs to source and support.
The second belongs to evolving state geometry.
The third belongs to fixed reference geometry.
The conventional Friedmann sum combines all three only after those distinct physical projections have already been constructed.
The central statement is therefore:


Central statement. The cosmological-constant term is not initially a primitive source density or a primitive cosmological arrow. It is a state-independent rate-squared contribution set by a fixed geometric reference scale. For positive \(\Lambda\), that scale can be written as the pure de Sitter reference area \(A_\Lambda\). Only afterward can the same contribution be represented as an \(\epsilon_\Lambda\) vacuum-energy density and attributed phenomenologically to dark energy. [The source PDF’s boxed version contains broken KaTeX placeholders; author review required.]

And hence:

Fixed reference area occurs before dark-energy attribution.

title: Addendum 64 — Source-Support Work Occurs Before Cosmological Acceleration
section: Abstract
text:
Abstract

Addenda 59–63 reconstructed the first Friedmann equation in successive physical layers.
Recursive throughput, geometric projection, and clock calibration supplied the physical rate
\[ H\]
The squared rate was then partitioned as
\[ H^2=F_\varepsilon+F_k+F_\Lambda, \]
where
\[ \begin{aligned}F_\varepsilon&=\frac{8\pi G}{3c^2}\varepsilon,\\F_k&=-\frac{kc^2}{a^2},\end{aligned} \]
and
\[ F_\Lambda=\frac{\Lambda c^2}{3}\]
These terms were subsequently deprojected.
The matter-energy contribution is a physical source-energy read divided by physical boundary support.
The curvature contribution is a state-dependent geometric read proportional to inverse boundary area.
The cosmological-constant contribution is a state-independent reference-geometric read.
The next question is therefore not:

What primitive R2D quantity is cosmological acceleration?


It is:

How does the already-defined physical cosmological rate change as its projected source and / geometric coordinates evolve?

Physical acceleration is
\[ \frac{\ddot a}{a}=\dot H+H^2. \]
Thus it occurs after the physical rate has already been defined.
For a homogeneous source, Addendum 61 gave the physical source-support relation
\[ dE=-p\,dV, \]
with
\[ E=\epsilon V\]
Because cosmological support scales as
\[ V\propto a^3, \]
this gives
\[\dot\epsilon+3H(\epsilon+p)=0\]
Differentiate the first Friedmann partition for a fixed gravitational projection class with constant
\[ G,\quad k,\quad\Lambda. \]
Then
\[2H\dot H=\dot F_\epsilon+\dot F_k+\dot F_\Lambda\]
The source term evolves through source-support work:
\[ \dot F_\varepsilon=-\frac{8\pi G}{c^2}H(\varepsilon+p). \]
The curvature term evolves through changing boundary geometry:
\[ \dot F_k=-2HF_k. \]
The constant reference term does not evolve:

ḞΛ = 0.
Therefore, on an interval with H ≠ 0,
\[\dot H=-\frac{4\pi G}{c^2}(\epsilon+p)-F_k\]
Using
\[ F_k=-\frac{kc^2}{a^2}\]
this is
\[\dot H=-\frac{4\pi G}{c^2}(\epsilon+p)+\frac{kc^2}{a^2}\]
Now add
\[ H^2=F_\epsilon+F_k+F_\Lambda\]
Then
\[\frac{\ddot a}{a}=-\frac{4\pi G}{c^2}(\epsilon+p)-F_k+F_\epsilon+F_k+F_\Lambda\]
The explicit curvature contribution cancels:
\[ -F_k+F_k=0. \]
Therefore,
\[\frac{\ddot a}{a}=-\frac{4\pi G}{3c^2}(\epsilon+3p)+\frac{\Lambda c^2}{3}\]
This is the conventional acceleration equation.
Its structure now has a clear physical ordering.
Pressure appears because source energy changes as three-dimensional boundary support changes.
Curvature disappears because it belongs to the instantaneous geometric rate constraint and evolves exactly with the state geometry.
The fixed reference term remains because its physical scale does not dilute with the evolving cosmological area.

The second Friedmann equation is therefore not an independent primitive cosmological cause inserted beside the first.
Within the fixed FLRW projection considered here, it follows from evolution of the already-defined rate partition together with physical source-support continuity.
The central statement is:
the cosmological acceleration equation is not a second primitive law acting beside the Friedmann rate constraint. Within a fixed FLRW projection, it follows from the evolution of that already-defined rate partition together with source-support work. Pressure enters because physical source energy changes with three-dimensional boundary support; spatial curvature cancels because it belongs to the evolving geometric state rather than to the active source.
And hence:

Source-support work occurs before cosmological acceleration.

section: 79. Conclusion
text:
79. Conclusion
The cosmological acceleration equation is often presented beside the first Friedmann equation as another fundamental dynamical statement.

The R2D reconstruction places it later.
The first Friedmann equation already describes the physical rate magnitude after recursive throughput has been projected into gravitational coordinates:
\[ H^2=F_\epsilon+F_k+F_\Lambda\]
Each contribution has different physical ownership.
Matter-energy is a source-energy/support relation.
Curvature is evolving state geometry.
The cosmological constant is fixed reference geometry.
Their derivatives therefore differ.
Source energy changes because the physical source does work against changing support:
\[ dE=-p\,dV\]
For three-dimensional homogeneous support,
\[ V\propto a^3\]
Consequently,
\[\dot\epsilon+3H(\epsilon+p)=0\]
Spatial curvature evolves as
\[\dot F_k=-2HF_k\]
The constant reference contribution satisfies
\[\dot F_\Lambda=0\]
Differentiating the first Friedmann equation therefore yields
\[\dot H=-\frac{4\pi G}{c^2}(\epsilon+p)+\frac{kc^2}{a^2}\]
When this rate evolution is combined with
\[\frac{\ddot a}{a}=\dot H+H^2\]

the curvature contribution cancels exactly.
The result is
\[\frac{\ddot a}{a}=-\frac{4\pi G}{3c^2}(\epsilon+3p)+\frac{\Lambda c^2}{3}\]
The familiar 3p contribution therefore appears because source energy responds to changing three- dimensional boundary support.
The absence of an explicit curvature term appears because spatial curvature belongs to the evolving state geometry already represented in the rate constraint.
The surviving Λ term appears because its reference scale does not dilute with the cosmological state area.
None of these quantities is primitive R2D asymmetry.
The primitive directional question has already been answered upstream.
The acceleration equation answers a later question:

How does the physically projected cosmological rate change as its source and geometric / reads evolve?

The central statement is therefore:
the cosmological acceleration equation is not a second primitive law acting beside the Friedmann rate constraint. Within a fixed FLRW projection, it follows from the evolution of that already-defined rate partition together with source-support work. Pressure enters because physical source energy changes with three-dimensional boundary support; spatial curvature cancels because it belongs to the evolving geometric state rather than to the active source.
And hence:

Source-support work occurs before cosmological acceleration.

title: Addendum 65 — Boundary-Area Scaling Occurs Before Cosmological Epochs
section: Abstract
text:
Abstract

Addenda 59–64 reconstructed cosmological dynamics in a layered R2D order.
Primitive directional asymmetry occurs before structural realization.
Recursive throughput occurs before physical rate.
Clock and geometric calibration produce the Hubble rate
\[ H\]
The first Friedmann equation then partitions the physical rate magnitude:
\[ H^2=F_\varepsilon+F_k+F_\Lambda. \]
Addenda 61–63 deprojected the individual terms.
Matter-energy is a source-energy read divided by physical boundary support.
Spatial curvature is an inverse-area geometric read of the evolving cosmological state.
A constant positive Λ is a fixed reference-geometric contribution.
Addendum 64 then showed that evolution of these already-defined physical reads produces the cosmological acceleration equation.
The next question is therefore:

Why does one cosmological history appear as successive radiation-, matter-, curvature-, and \(\Lambda\)-dominated epochs?

R2D does not require a different primitive law for each epoch.
Nor does a change of dominant Friedmann contribution necessarily imply recursive boundary replacement.

The distinction follows from the different ways in which downstream physical reads scale with the same evolving cosmological boundary area.
For a separately conserved homogeneous source component j with constant equation-of-state parameter
\[ p_j=w_j\varepsilon_j, \]
source continuity gives
\[ \varepsilon_j\propto a^{-3(1+w_j)}. \]
Since the cosmological boundary-area read satisfies
\[ A_\zeta\propto a^2, \]
the corresponding Friedmann contribution obeys
\[ F_j(A_\zeta)=B_j A_\zeta^{-s_j}, \]
with
\[ s_j=\frac{3}{2}(1+w_j). \]
Thus radiation has
\[ s_r=2, \]
pressureless matter has
\[ s_m=\frac32, \]
spatial curvature has the geometric scaling
\[ s_k=1, \]
and constant Λ has
\[ s_\Lambda=0. \]
The familiar hierarchy is therefore
\[2>\frac32>1>0\]
On an expanding branch,

Ȧζ > 0,
so contributions with larger scaling exponent decrease more rapidly.
Radiation therefore falls relative to matter.
Matter falls relative to curvature magnitude.
Matter and curvature both fall relative to a constant Λ contribution.
The cosmological history is consequently a history of changing relative weights within one physical rate partition.
Define a reference area
\[ A_0\]
and write
\[ F_j(A)=F_{j,0}\left(\frac{A}{A_0}\right)^{-s_j}\]
For two positive contributions i and j , their equality occurs at
\[ A_{i\mid j}=A_0\left(\frac{F_{i,0}}{F_{j,0}}\right)^{1/(s_i-s_j)}. \]
This defines an equality area.
Matter-radiation equality, matter-Λ equality, and analogous crossovers are therefore not intrinsically new count boundaries.
They are values of the same cosmological boundary area at which two downstream physical contributions to \(H^2\) become equal.
The normalized partition weights can be defined by
\[ \Omega_j=\frac{F_j}{H^2}, \]
with
\[\sum_j\Omega_j=1\]
For fixed area-scaling exponents,

dFj
\[\frac{dF_j}{d\ln A_\zeta}=-s_jF_j\]
Define the signed partition-weighted scaling exponent
\[\bar s=\sum_\ell s_\ell\Omega_\ell\]
Then the normalized contributions obey
\[\frac{d\Omega_j}{d\ln A_\zeta}=\Omega_j(\bar s-s_j)\]
This is a compact physical equation for the evolution of the Friedmann partition.
On an expanding branch, positive contributions with
\[ s_j > \bar s\]
lose relative weight, while those with
\[ s_j < \bar s\]
gain relative weight.
The equation is not a new primitive R2D law.
It is the downstream consequence of one evolving boundary area acting on physical reads that carry different scaling exponents.
This also separates several transitions that are often conflated.
Partition equality,
\[ F_i = F_j\]
is not the same as cosmological acceleration onset,
\[\ddot a = 0\]
which is not the same as a turning point,
\[ H = 0\]
and none is automatically primitive R2D stall,
\[ A_\zeta = 0\]

For pressureless matter plus positive constant Λ, matter-Λ equality occurs when
\[\epsilon_m = \epsilon_\Lambda\]
Acceleration begins earlier, when
\[\epsilon_m = 2\epsilon_\Lambda\]
Because
\[\epsilon_m\propto A_\zeta^{-3/2}\]
the acceleration-threshold area satisfies
\[ A_{\mathrm{acc}}=2^{-2/3}A_{m\mid\Lambda}\]
Thus accelerated expansion begins before the Λ contribution becomes larger than the matter contribution to \(H^2\).
Dominance and acceleration are different physical statements.
The central result is therefore:
cosmological epochs are not successive primitive laws or necessarily successive recursive boundaries. They are regimes in which different physical projections of one cosmological boundary dominate the Friedmann rate partition because those projections scale differently with the evolving boundary area. Equality epochs are therefore equality areas within one projected history.
And hence:

boundary-area scaling occurs before cosmological epochs.

title: Addendum 65 — Boundary-Area Scaling Occurs Before Cosmological Epochs
section: 1. Cosmological History Begins With One Evolving Boundary
text:
1. Cosmological History Begins With One Evolving Boundary
Let
\[ B_\zeta\]
denote the cosmological boundary under reconstruction.
Its structural state changes within the same boundary:
\[ i_\zeta^\ast \to  k_\zeta^\ast \to  \cdots\]
and its physical boundary-area read changes correspondingly:
\[ A_{\zeta,1} \to  A_{\zeta,2} \to  \cdots\]
Nothing in this sequence requires recursive replacement of Bζ .
crumbs: Addenda
46  Addendum 65 — Boundary-Area Scaling Occurs Before Cosmological Epochs

title: Addendum 65 — Boundary-Area Scaling Occurs Before Cosmological Epochs
section: 2. The Friedmann Partition Evolves on That Boundary
text:
2. The Friedmann Partition Evolves on That Boundary
The projected physical rate satisfies
\[ H^2=\sum_j F_j\]
The relative magnitude of the terms can change as
\[ A_\zeta\]
changes.
Thus the physical interpretation of the history can change while the underlying boundary ownership remains the same.
crumbs: Addenda
46  Addendum 65 — Boundary-Area Scaling Occurs Before Cosmological Epochs

title: Addendum 65 — Boundary-Area Scaling Occurs Before Cosmological Epochs
section: 3. Define a Projected Dominance Regime
text:
3. Define a Projected Dominance Regime
A physical contribution j dominates over a range of area when
\[|F_j|\gg|F_\ell|\]
for the other dynamically relevant terms \(\ell\).
A cosmological “epoch” can therefore be defined as a dominance regime of the projected rate partition.
crumbs: Addenda
46  Addendum 65 — Boundary-Area Scaling Occurs Before Cosmological Epochs

title: Addendum 65 — Boundary-Area Scaling Occurs Before Cosmological Epochs
section: 4. Epoch Does Not Mean Primitive Ontology
text:
4. Epoch Does Not Mean Primitive Ontology
A radiation-dominated regime does not imply that the primitive universe has become “radiation.”
A matter-dominated regime does not imply that a new primitive matter law has replaced it.
A Λ-dominated regime does not imply that terminal R2D causality has become Λ.
The names identify which downstream physical read dominates the projected rate.
crumbs: Addenda
46  Addendum 65 — Boundary-Area Scaling Occurs Before Cosmological Epochs

title: Addendum 65 — Boundary-Area Scaling Occurs Before Cosmological Epochs
section: 5. General Source Scaling Comes From Source Continuity
text:
5. General Source Scaling Comes From Source Continuity
For a separately conserved homogeneous source component,

pj = wj εj .
The continuity equation is
\[\dot\epsilon_j+3H(\epsilon_j+p_j)=0\]
crumbs: Addenda
46  Addendum 65 — Boundary-Area Scaling Occurs Before Cosmological Epochs

title: Addendum 65 — Boundary-Area Scaling Occurs Before Cosmological Epochs
section: 6. Substitute the Equation of State
text:
6. Substitute the Equation of State
Then
\[\dot\epsilon_j+3H(1+w_j)\epsilon_j=0\]
Therefore:
\[\epsilon_j\propto a^{-3(1+w_j)}\]
crumbs: Addenda
46  Addendum 65 — Boundary-Area Scaling Occurs Before Cosmological Epochs

title: Addendum 65 — Boundary-Area Scaling Occurs Before Cosmological Epochs
section: 7. Replace Scale Factor With Boundary Area
text:
7. Replace Scale Factor With Boundary Area
Because
\[ A_\zeta\propto a^2,\qquad a\propto A_\zeta^{1/2}\]
Thus:
\[\epsilon_j\propto A_\zeta^{-\frac32(1+w_j)}\]
crumbs: Addenda
46  Addendum 65 — Boundary-Area Scaling Occurs Before Cosmological Epochs

title: Addendum 65 — Boundary-Area Scaling Occurs Before Cosmological Epochs
section: 8. Define the Area-Scaling Exponent
text:
8. Define the Area-Scaling Exponent
Let
\[ s_j\equiv\frac32(1+w_j)\]
Then:
\[ F_j\propto A_\zeta^{-s_j}\]
For ordinary positive-energy source terms, the gravitational prefactor does not change the area exponent.
crumbs: Addenda
46  Addendum 65 — Boundary-Area Scaling Occurs Before Cosmological Epochs

title: Addendum 65 — Boundary-Area Scaling Occurs Before Cosmological Epochs
section: 9. Radiation Has sr = 2
text:
9. Radiation Has sr = 2
For radiation,
\[ w_r=\frac13\]
Therefore:
\[ s_r=\frac32\left(1+\frac13\right)=2\]
Hence:
\[ F_r\propto A_\zeta^{-2}\]
crumbs: Addenda
46  Addendum 65 — Boundary-Area Scaling Occurs Before Cosmological Epochs

title: Addendum 65 — Boundary-Area Scaling Occurs Before Cosmological Epochs
section: 10. Matter Has sm = 3/2
text:
10. Matter Has sm = 3/2
For pressureless matter,
\[ w_m = 0\]
Therefore:
\[ s_m=\frac32\]
Thus:
\[ F_m\propto A_\zeta^{-3/2}\]
This is the result already obtained directly from source energy divided by boundary support.
crumbs: Addenda
46  Addendum 65 — Boundary-Area Scaling Occurs Before Cosmological Epochs

title: Addendum 65 — Boundary-Area Scaling Occurs Before Cosmological Epochs
section: 11. Curvature Has Effective Scaling Exponent One
text:
11. Curvature Has Effective Scaling Exponent One
Addendum 62 gave
\[ F_k\propto A_\zeta^{-1}\]
Thus define its geometric area-scaling exponent as
\[ s_k = 1\]

This notation does not make curvature a physical fluid.
crumbs: Addenda
46  Addendum 65 — Boundary-Area Scaling Occurs Before Cosmological Epochs

title: Addendum 65 — Boundary-Area Scaling Occurs Before Cosmological Epochs
section: 12. Constant Λ Has Scaling Exponent Zero
text:
12. Constant Λ Has Scaling Exponent Zero
Addendum 63 gave
\[ F_\Lambda=\mathrm{constant}\]
Therefore:
\[ s_\Lambda = 0\]
crumbs: Addenda
46  Addendum 65 — Boundary-Area Scaling Occurs Before Cosmological Epochs

title: Addendum 65 — Boundary-Area Scaling Occurs Before Cosmological Epochs
section: 13. The Standard Scaling Hierarchy Is
text:
13. The Standard Scaling Hierarchy Is
\[ s_r>s_m>s_k>s_\Lambda\]
Explicitly,
\[2>\frac32>1>0\]
crumbs: Addenda
46  Addendum 65 — Boundary-Area Scaling Occurs Before Cosmological Epochs

title: Addendum 65 — Boundary-Area Scaling Occurs Before Cosmological Epochs
section: 14. This Hierarchy Is an Area Hierarchy
text:
14. This Hierarchy Is an Area Hierarchy
The familiar scale-factor powers
\[ a^{-4},\quad a^{-3},\quad a^{-2},\quad a^0\]
become
\[ A_\zeta^{-2},\quad A_\zeta^{-3/2},\quad A_\zeta^{-1},\quad A_\zeta^0\]
Boundary area is therefore sufficient to order the sectors.
crumbs: Addenda
46  Addendum 65 — Boundary-Area Scaling Occurs Before Cosmological Epochs

title: Addendum 65 — Boundary-Area Scaling Occurs Before Cosmological Epochs
section: 15. Expansion Makes Large-s Terms Fade Faster
text:
15. Expansion Makes Large-s Terms Fade Faster
For an expanding branch,
\[\dot A_\zeta > 0\]
If

si > sj ,
then
\[\frac{|F_i|}{|F_j|}\propto A_\zeta^{-(s_i-s_j)}\]
decreases with area.
crumbs: Addenda
46  Addendum 65 — Boundary-Area Scaling Occurs Before Cosmological Epochs

title: Addendum 65 — Boundary-Area Scaling Occurs Before Cosmological Epochs
section: 16. Radiation Falls Relative to Matter
text:
16. Radiation Falls Relative to Matter
Because
\[ s_r-s_m=\frac12,\qquad\frac{F_r}{F_m}\propto A_\zeta^{-1/2}\]
Thus radiation naturally becomes less important relative to matter as an expanding boundary grows.
crumbs: Addenda
46  Addendum 65 — Boundary-Area Scaling Occurs Before Cosmological Epochs

title: Addendum 65 — Boundary-Area Scaling Occurs Before Cosmological Epochs
section: 17. Matter Falls Relative to Curvature Magnitude
text:
17. Matter Falls Relative to Curvature Magnitude
Similarly,
\[ s_m-s_k=\frac12\]
so
\[\frac{F_m}{|F_k|}\propto A_\zeta^{-1/2}\]
Where curvature is dynamically relevant, its magnitude falls more slowly than matter.
crumbs: Addenda
46  Addendum 65 — Boundary-Area Scaling Occurs Before Cosmological Epochs

title: Addendum 65 — Boundary-Area Scaling Occurs Before Cosmological Epochs
section: 18. Matter Falls More Rapidly Relative to Λ
text:
18. Matter Falls More Rapidly Relative to Λ
Because
\[ s_m-s_\Lambda=\frac32,\qquad\frac{F_m}{F_\Lambda}\propto A_\zeta^{-3/2}\]
crumbs: Addenda
46  Addendum 65 — Boundary-Area Scaling Occurs Before Cosmological Epochs

title: Addendum 65 — Boundary-Area Scaling Occurs Before Cosmological Epochs
section: 19. Radiation Falls Even More Rapidly Relative to Λ
text:
19. Radiation Falls Even More Rapidly Relative to Λ
Because
\[ s_r - s_\Lambda = 2\]
\[\frac{F_r}{F_\Lambda}\propto A_\zeta^{-2}\]
crumbs: Addenda
46  Addendum 65 — Boundary-Area Scaling Occurs Before Cosmological Epochs

title: Addendum 65 — Boundary-Area Scaling Occurs Before Cosmological Epochs
section: 20. Curvature Falls Relative to a Constant Reference Contribution
text:
20. Curvature Falls Relative to a Constant Reference Contribution
Since
\[ s_k - s_\Lambda = 1\]
\[\frac{|F_k|}{F_\Lambda}\propto A_\zeta^{-1}\]
crumbs: Addenda
46  Addendum 65 — Boundary-Area Scaling Occurs Before Cosmological Epochs

title: Addendum 65 — Boundary-Area Scaling Occurs Before Cosmological Epochs
section: 21. The Ordering Is Conditional on the Coefficients
text:
21. The Ordering Is Conditional on the Coefficients
Scaling exponents determine how relative contributions change.
They do not determine their absolute amplitudes.
A sector with a negligible coefficient may never dominate over the physical interval being considered.
crumbs: Addenda
46  Addendum 65 — Boundary-Area Scaling Occurs Before Cosmological Epochs

title: Addendum 65 — Boundary-Area Scaling Occurs Before Cosmological Epochs
section: 22. Therefore the Standard Epoch Sequence Is Not Mathematically Mandatory
text:
22. Therefore the Standard Epoch Sequence Is Not Mathematically Mandatory
The exponent ordering permits a typical progression from rapidly diluting sectors toward slowly diluting sectors.
But it does not guarantee a distinct curvature-dominated era, for example.
Physical calibration and initial partition weights matter.
crumbs: Addenda
46  Addendum 65 — Boundary-Area Scaling Occurs Before Cosmological Epochs

title: Addendum 65 — Boundary-Area Scaling Occurs Before Cosmological Epochs
section: 23. Define a Reference-Area Representation
text:
23. Define a Reference-Area Representation
Choose some physical reference state with area
\[ A_0\]
Write:
\[ F_j(A)=F_{j,0}\left(\frac{A}{A_0}\right)^{-s_j}\]
This representation makes crossover areas explicit.
crumbs: Addenda
46  Addendum 65 — Boundary-Area Scaling Occurs Before Cosmological Epochs

title: Addendum 65 — Boundary-Area Scaling Occurs Before Cosmological Epochs
section: 24. Equality of Two Positive Contributions
text:
24. Equality of Two Positive Contributions
Suppose i and j are positive contributions with
\[ s_i\ne s_j\]
Their equality condition is
\[ F_i = F_j\]
crumbs: Addenda
46  Addendum 65 — Boundary-Area Scaling Occurs Before Cosmological Epochs

title: Addendum 65 — Boundary-Area Scaling Occurs Before Cosmological Epochs
section: 25. Solve for the Equality Area
text:
25. Solve for the Equality Area
Then:
\[ F_{i,0}\left(\frac{A}{A_0}\right)^{-s_i}=F_{j,0}\left(\frac{A}{A_0}\right)^{-s_j}\]
Therefore:
\[ A_{i\mid j}=A_0\left(\frac{F_{i,0}}{F_{j,0}}\right)^{1/(s_i-s_j)}\]
crumbs: Addenda
46  Addendum 65 — Boundary-Area Scaling Occurs Before Cosmological Epochs

title: Addendum 65 — Boundary-Area Scaling Occurs Before Cosmological Epochs
section: 26. Equality Time Is Therefore Downstream of Equality Area
text:
26. Equality Time Is Therefore Downstream of Equality Area
Once a physical clock and cosmological solution
\[ A_\zeta (t)\]
are supplied, one may assign a time

ti∣j
to the equality event.
But the geometric crossover condition itself is already defined by
\[ A_{i\mid j}\]
Thus:
\[\text{equality area}\to\text{equality time read}\]
crumbs: Addenda
46  Addendum 65 — Boundary-Area Scaling Occurs Before Cosmological Epochs

title: Addendum 65 — Boundary-Area Scaling Occurs Before Cosmological Epochs
section: 27. Matter-Radiation Equality Is an Equality Area
text:
27. Matter-Radiation Equality Is an Equality Area
For radiation and matter,
\[ s_r-s_m=\frac12\]
Thus:
\[ A_{r\mid m}=A_0\left(\frac{F_{r,0}}{F_{m,0}}\right)^2\]
crumbs: Addenda
46  Addendum 65 — Boundary-Area Scaling Occurs Before Cosmological Epochs

title: Addendum 65 — Boundary-Area Scaling Occurs Before Cosmological Epochs
section: 28. Nothing Recursively Closes at Matter-Radiation Equality by Definition
text:
28. Nothing Recursively Closes at Matter-Radiation Equality by Definition
The condition is simply
\[ F_r = F_m\]
It does not imply
\[ B_\zeta \to  B_{\zeta+1}\]
crumbs: Addenda
46  Addendum 65 — Boundary-Area Scaling Occurs Before Cosmological Epochs

title: Addendum 65 — Boundary-Area Scaling Occurs Before Cosmological Epochs
section: 29. Nor Does It Require a Change in Primitive R2D Law
text:
29. Nor Does It Require a Change in Primitive R2D Law
The same primitive architecture continues to apply on both sides of the crossover.
Only the dominant physical projection changes.
crumbs: Addenda
46  Addendum 65 — Boundary-Area Scaling Occurs Before Cosmological Epochs

title: Addendum 65 — Boundary-Area Scaling Occurs Before Cosmological Epochs
section: 30. Matter-Λ Equality Is Likewise an Equality Area
text:
30. Matter-Λ Equality Is Likewise an Equality Area
For matter,
\[ s_m=\frac32\]
while
\[ s_\Lambda = 0\]
Therefore:
\[ A_{m\mid\Lambda}=A_0\left(\frac{F_{m,0}}{F_\Lambda}\right)^{2/3}\]
crumbs: Addenda
46  Addendum 65 — Boundary-Area Scaling Occurs Before Cosmological Epochs

title: Addendum 65 — Boundary-Area Scaling Occurs Before Cosmological Epochs
section: 31. The Λ Reference Scale Does Not Change at Equality
text:
31. The Λ Reference Scale Does Not Change at Equality
At
\[ A_{m\mid\Lambda}\]
the evolving matter contribution has fallen to the fixed Λ contribution.
The reference area
\[ A_\Lambda\]
itself has not changed.
crumbs: Addenda
46  Addendum 65 — Boundary-Area Scaling Occurs Before Cosmological Epochs

title: Addendum 65 — Boundary-Area Scaling Occurs Before Cosmological Epochs
section: 32. Curvature Equality Requires Sign Care
text:
32. Curvature Equality Requires Sign Care
The curvature contribution is
\[ F_k=-\frac{kc^2}{a^2}\]
Thus its sign depends on the curvature class.
A generic “curvature dominance” statement should therefore distinguish magnitude from signed contribution.
crumbs: Addenda
46  Addendum 65 — Boundary-Area Scaling Occurs Before Cosmological Epochs

title: Addendum 65 — Boundary-Area Scaling Occurs Before Cosmological Epochs
section: 33. For Crossover Magnitudes Use
text:
33. For Crossover Magnitudes Use
\[|F_k|\]
For example,
\[|F_k|=F_\Lambda\]
defines a curvature-Λ magnitude-equality area.
crumbs: Addenda
46  Addendum 65 — Boundary-Area Scaling Occurs Before Cosmological Epochs

title: Addendum 65 — Boundary-Area Scaling Occurs Before Cosmological Epochs
section: 34. For Closed Positive-Curvature Geometry, Cancellation Is Possible
text:
34. For Closed Positive-Curvature Geometry, Cancellation Is Possible
When
\[ k = +1\]
\[ F_k < 0\]
A negative curvature contribution can partially cancel positive source terms.
Thus the relevant event may be a rate reduction or turning point rather than a positive-sector dominance regime.
crumbs: Addenda
46  Addendum 65 — Boundary-Area Scaling Occurs Before Cosmological Epochs

title: Addendum 65 — Boundary-Area Scaling Occurs Before Cosmological Epochs
section: 35. A Turning Point Is Defined by the Whole Partition
text:
35. A Turning Point Is Defined by the Whole Partition
A cosmological turning point satisfies
\[ H = 0\]
Therefore:
\[\sum_jF_j=0\]
This is not the same condition as equality of any arbitrary pair of contributions.
crumbs: Addenda
46  Addendum 65 — Boundary-Area Scaling Occurs Before Cosmological Epochs

title: Addendum 65 — Boundary-Area Scaling Occurs Before Cosmological Epochs
section: 36. Partition Equality Is Not a Turning Point
text:
36. Partition Equality Is Not a Turning Point
The condition
\[ F_i = F_j\]

usually occurs while
\[ H^2 > 0\]
Thus:
\[\text{partition equality}\ne\text{turning point}\]
crumbs: Addenda
46  Addendum 65 — Boundary-Area Scaling Occurs Before Cosmological Epochs

title: Addendum 65 — Boundary-Area Scaling Occurs Before Cosmological Epochs
section: 37. Partition Equality Is Also Not R2D Stall
text:
37. Partition Equality Is Also Not R2D Stall
Primitive R2D stall is
\[ A_\zeta = 0\]
No derivation equates this with
\[ F_i = F_j\]
Therefore:
\[\text{equality area}\ne\text{primitive stall}\]
by definition.
crumbs: Addenda
46  Addendum 65 — Boundary-Area Scaling Occurs Before Cosmological Epochs

title: Addendum 65 — Boundary-Area Scaling Occurs Before Cosmological Epochs
section: 38. Nor Is Equality Automatically a Structural Macrostate Transition
text:
38. Nor Is Equality Automatically a Structural Macrostate Transition
A change in which Friedmann term is larger does not necessarily imply that the occupancy mode
\[ i_\zeta^\ast\]
has changed.
The partition and structural-state descriptions belong to different layers.
crumbs: Addenda
46  Addendum 65 — Boundary-Area Scaling Occurs Before Cosmological Epochs

title: Addendum 65 — Boundary-Area Scaling Occurs Before Cosmological Epochs
section: 39. Define Normalized Friedmann Contributions
text:
39. Define Normalized Friedmann Contributions
For
\[ H^2 \ne 0\]
define

Fj
\[\Omega_j=\frac{F_j}{H^2}\]
Then:
\[\sum_j\Omega_j=1\]
These are signed physical partition weights.
crumbs: Addenda
46  Addendum 65 — Boundary-Area Scaling Occurs Before Cosmological Epochs

title: Addendum 65 — Boundary-Area Scaling Occurs Before Cosmological Epochs
section: 40. The Ωj Are Not Probabilities
text:
40. The Ωj Are Not Probabilities
They are not:
\[ W_j/W_{\mathrm{tot}}\]
not occupancies,
and not R2D possibility fractions.
They are normalized contributions to the projected rate constraint.
crumbs: Addenda
46  Addendum 65 — Boundary-Area Scaling Occurs Before Cosmological Epochs

title: Addendum 65 — Boundary-Area Scaling Occurs Before Cosmological Epochs
section: 41. Differentiate One Scaling Sector
text:
41. Differentiate One Scaling Sector
For
\[ F_j=B_jA^{-s_j}\]
\[\frac{dF_j}{d\ln A}=-s_jF_j\]
crumbs: Addenda
46  Addendum 65 — Boundary-Area Scaling Occurs Before Cosmological Epochs

title: Addendum 65 — Boundary-Area Scaling Occurs Before Cosmological Epochs
section: 42. Differentiate the Total Rate Magnitude
text:
42. Differentiate the Total Rate Magnitude
Since
\[ H^2=\sum_\ell F_\ell\]
\[\frac{dH^2}{d\ln A}=-\sum_\ell s_\ell F_\ell\]
crumbs: Addenda
46  Addendum 65 — Boundary-Area Scaling Occurs Before Cosmological Epochs

title: Addendum 65 — Boundary-Area Scaling Occurs Before Cosmological Epochs
section: 43. Define the Partition-Weighted Scaling Exponent
text:
43. Define the Partition-Weighted Scaling Exponent
Let
\[\bar s=\sum_\ell s_\ell\Omega_\ell\]
Then:
\[\frac{d\ln H^2}{d\ln A}=-\bar s\]

The weighted exponent \(\bar s\) is algebraic and need not be a convex average. For signed contributions, s average.
crumbs: Addenda
46  Addendum 65 — Boundary-Area Scaling Occurs Before Cosmological Epochs

title: Addendum 65 — Boundary-Area Scaling Occurs Before Cosmological Epochs
section: 44. Derive the Partition-Flow Equation
text:
44. Derive the Partition-Flow Equation
Differentiate
\[\Omega_j=\frac{F_j}{H^2}\]
Then:
\[\frac{d\Omega_j}{d\ln A_\zeta}=\Omega_j(\bar s-s_j)\]
crumbs: Addenda
46  Addendum 65 — Boundary-Area Scaling Occurs Before Cosmological Epochs

title: Addendum 65 — Boundary-Area Scaling Occurs Before Cosmological Epochs
section: 45. This Describes the Evolution of Cosmological Dominance
text:
45. This Describes the Evolution of Cosmological Dominance
For positive contributions on an expanding branch:
If
\[ s_j > \bar s\]
then
\[\frac{d\Omega_j}{d\ln A}<0\]
Its relative importance falls.
crumbs: Addenda
46  Addendum 65 — Boundary-Area Scaling Occurs Before Cosmological Epochs

title: Addendum 65 — Boundary-Area Scaling Occurs Before Cosmological Epochs
section: 46. If sj < s ˉ
text:
46. If sj < s ˉ
then
\[\frac{d\Omega_j}{d\ln A}>0\]
Its relative importance grows.
crumbs: Addenda
46  Addendum 65 — Boundary-Area Scaling Occurs Before Cosmological Epochs

title: Addendum 65 — Boundary-Area Scaling Occurs Before Cosmological Epochs
section: 47. Constant Contributions Naturally Gain Relative Weight
text:
47. Constant Contributions Naturally Gain Relative Weight
For constant Λ,
\[ s_\Lambda = 0\]
While other positive sectors have
\[ s_j > 0\]
the Λ partition fraction tends to grow as an expanding boundary increases in area.
crumbs: Addenda
46  Addendum 65 — Boundary-Area Scaling Occurs Before Cosmological Epochs

title: Addendum 65 — Boundary-Area Scaling Occurs Before Cosmological Epochs
section: 48. Radiation Naturally Loses Relative Weight
text:
48. Radiation Naturally Loses Relative Weight
Radiation has the largest standard exponent,
\[ s_r = 2\]
It therefore declines most rapidly among the usual positive sectors as area grows.
crumbs: Addenda
46  Addendum 65 — Boundary-Area Scaling Occurs Before Cosmological Epochs

title: Addendum 65 — Boundary-Area Scaling Occurs Before Cosmological Epochs
section: 49. Matter Lies Between Radiation and the Nondiluting Sector
text:
49. Matter Lies Between Radiation and the Nondiluting Sector
With
\[ s_m=\frac32\]
matter decreases more slowly than radiation but more quickly than curvature magnitude or constant Λ.
Its intermediate dominance is therefore a scaling consequence where amplitudes permit it.
crumbs: Addenda
46  Addendum 65 — Boundary-Area Scaling Occurs Before Cosmological Epochs

title: Addendum 65 — Boundary-Area Scaling Occurs Before Cosmological Epochs
section: 50. The Partition-Flow Equation Is Not a Primitive R2D Evolution Law
text:
50. The Partition-Flow Equation Is Not a Primitive R2D Evolution Law
It follows only after:

• physical source classes have been defined; • geometric curvature has been projected; • a fixed Λ reference scale has been supplied; • the first Friedmann rate partition has been formed.

Thus it belongs entirely to the mature cosmological projection.
crumbs: Addenda
46  Addendum 65 — Boundary-Area Scaling Occurs Before Cosmological Epochs

title: Addendum 65 — Boundary-Area Scaling Occurs Before Cosmological Epochs
section: 51. Dominance and Acceleration Must Be Separated
text:
51. Dominance and Acceleration Must Be Separated
Addendum 64 showed that acceleration depends on
\[\epsilon + 3p\]
rather than on which term is simply largest in \(H^2\).
Therefore the onset of accelerated expansion need not coincide with a Friedmann equality event.
crumbs: Addenda
46  Addendum 65 — Boundary-Area Scaling Occurs Before Cosmological Epochs

title: Addendum 65 — Boundary-Area Scaling Occurs Before Cosmological Epochs
section: 52. Consider Pressureless Matter Plus Constant Λ
text:
52. Consider Pressureless Matter Plus Constant Λ
Matter-Λ equality is
\[\epsilon_m = \epsilon_\Lambda\]
Equivalently,
\[ F_m = F_\Lambda\]
crumbs: Addenda
46  Addendum 65 — Boundary-Area Scaling Occurs Before Cosmological Epochs

title: Addendum 65 — Boundary-Area Scaling Occurs Before Cosmological Epochs
section: 53. The Acceleration Threshold Is Different
text:
53. The Acceleration Threshold Is Different
For pressureless matter plus Λ,
\[\frac{\ddot a}{a}=-\frac{4\pi G}{3c^2}\epsilon_m+\frac{\Lambda c^2}{3}\]
Using
\[\epsilon_\Lambda=\frac{\Lambda c^4}{8\pi G}\]

the acceleration threshold is
\[\epsilon_m = 2\epsilon_\Lambda\]
crumbs: Addenda
46  Addendum 65 — Boundary-Area Scaling Occurs Before Cosmological Epochs

title: Addendum 65 — Boundary-Area Scaling Occurs Before Cosmological Epochs
section: 54. Acceleration Therefore Begins Before Matter-Λ Equality on an Expanding Branch
text:
54. Acceleration Therefore Begins Before Matter-Λ Equality on an Expanding Branch
Matter density decreases as
\[\epsilon_m\propto A_\zeta^{-3/2}\]
Let
\[ A_{m\mid\Lambda}\]
denote matter-Λ equality.
Then:
\[\left(\frac{A_{\mathrm{acc}}}{A_{m\mid\Lambda}}\right)^{-3/2}=2\]
Hence:
\[ A_{\mathrm{acc}}=2^{-2/3}A_{m\mid\Lambda}\]
crumbs: Addenda
46  Addendum 65 — Boundary-Area Scaling Occurs Before Cosmological Epochs

title: Addendum 65 — Boundary-Area Scaling Occurs Before Cosmological Epochs
section: 55. Therefore
text:
55. Therefore
\[ A_{\mathrm{acc}}<A_{m\mid\Lambda}\]
on the expanding branch.

section: 77. Conclusion
text:
77. Conclusion
The conventional history of the universe is commonly divided into eras.
Radiation dominates early.
Matter later becomes dominant.
Curvature may become dynamically relevant.
A constant-Λ contribution can dominate at sufficiently large scale factor.
R2D does not require a new primitive law at each transition.
The same cosmological boundary can support all of these regimes.
What changes is the physical boundary area.
Each downstream physical sector responds differently to that change.
For a conserved constant-w source,
\[ F_j\propto A_\zeta^{-\frac32(1+w_j)}\]
Radiation therefore scales as
\[ F_r\propto A_\zeta^{-2}\]
Matter scales as

\[ A_\zeta^{-3/2}\]
Spatial curvature scales as
\[ F_k\propto A_\zeta^{-1}\]
Constant Λ scales as
\[ A_\zeta^0\]
The familiar cosmic sequence therefore emerges from a hierarchy of area-scaling exponents:
\[2>\frac32>1>0\]
As an expanding boundary grows, rapidly declining sectors lose relative importance and more slowly declining sectors gain it.
Two sectors become equal at a definite boundary area,
\[ A_{i\mid j}=A_0\left(\frac{F_{i,0}}{F_{j,0}}\right)^{1/(s_i-s_j)}\]
That is an equality area.
A later physical clock projection assigns it an equality time.
The crossover itself does not require a new recursive boundary.
Nor does it require a new primitive cosmological law.
The normalized physical partition obeys
\[\frac{d\Omega_j}{d\ln A_\zeta}=\Omega_j(\bar s-s_j)\]
Cosmological history is therefore readable as the changing relative weight of different physical projections along one evolving boundary-area trajectory.
This perspective also prevents several distinct events from being conflated.
Matter-Λ equality is not the onset of acceleration.
For pressureless matter and constant Λ,

Aacc = 2−2/3 Am∣Λ .
Acceleration begins before matter and \(\Lambda\) contribute equally to \(H^2\).
Partition equality is likewise not a turning point.
A turning point requires
\[ H = 0\]
And neither condition is primitive R2D stall,
\[ A_\zeta = 0\]
The layers remain distinct.
The deepest ordering is therefore not

radiation universe → matter universe → dark-energy universe.

It is:

one recursively organized cosmological boundary

whose downstream physical contributions possess different area-scaling laws and therefore exchange dominance as its projected area changes.
The central statement is therefore:
cosmological epochs are not successive primitive laws or necessarily successive recursive boundaries. They are regimes in which different physical projections of one cosmological boundary dominate the Friedmann rate partition because those projections scale differently with the evolving boundary area. Equality epochs are therefore equality areas within one projected history.
And hence:

boundary-area scaling occurs before cosmological epochs.

title: Addendum 66 — Recursive Realization Occurs Before the Big-Bang Projection
section: Abstract
text:
Abstract

Addendum 65 expressed cosmological history as changing dominance among physical Friedmann sectors along one evolving cosmological boundary-area trajectory.
For a physical sector j ,
\[ F_j(A_\zeta)=B_j A_\zeta^{-s_j}, \]
with the standard area-scaling exponents
\[ s_r=2,\qquad s_m=\frac32,\qquad s_k=1,\qquad s_\Lambda=0\]
Backward continuation of these fixed physical scaling laws produces the conventional FLRW singularity.
For any fixed nonzero comoving comparison domain,
\[ A_\zeta\propto a^2. \]
Thus:
\[ a\to0\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad A_\zeta\to0\]
The physical support volume then satisfies
\[ V_\zeta\propto A_\zeta^{3/2}\to0. \]
Matter density diverges:
\[ \varepsilon_m\propto A_\zeta^{-3/2}\to\infty. \]
Radiation density diverges more rapidly:
\[ \varepsilon_r\propto A_\zeta^{-2}\to\infty. \]
And, under the standard hot-source continuation,

∣H∣ → ∞.
These divergences are real properties of the extrapolated FLRW projection.
R2D does not deny the mathematics.
It denies the ontology conventionally assigned to its singular endpoint.
The singular Big Bang treats the backward limit of a later physical geometry as the primitive origin of reality:
\[ A\to0,\qquad V\to0,\qquad\epsilon\to\infty,\qquad|H|\to\infty\]
Everything is thereby assigned to an arbitrarily small physical support and the divergent endpoint is interpreted as the beginning.
R2D has the opposite causal architecture.
The largest presently realized gear is not an initially structureless point that subsequently acquires distinctions.
It is realized recursively through an infinitude of fundamental distinctions.
Those distinctions are not an infinite physical density packed into vanishing space.
Space, volume, density, temperature, curvature, and the scale factor are later physical reads of recursively organized distinction.
Thus:

[Archive box damaged: an infinitude of fundamental distinctions is distinct from divergent projected density. Author review required.]

The R2D hierarchy proceeds from primitive distinction through recursive realization:
fundamental distinctions \(\to\) subordinate closures \(\to\) recursive replacement \(\to\cdots\to B_\star\).
The largest gear \(B_\star\) is realized by this accumulated recursive organization.
Its existence is therefore not explained by extrapolating a geometric radius, scale factor, or volume backward toward zero.
Those quantities do not yet exist at the primitive level.
The singular Big-Bang ontology consequently reverses the R2D explanatory order.
It begins with the downstream projection,

a(t),
runs that projection backward to
\[ a = 0\]
and identifies the endpoint with the origin of the distinctions from which the projection itself was constructed.
R2D rejects that inversion.
The hot thermal cosmological state remains physically meaningful.
A radiation-dominated universe, thermal background, decreasing temperature under expansion, and the later cosmological history reconstructed from those physical reads can all belong to a realized cosmological boundary.
But the hot thermal boundary occurs inside an already realized recursive hierarchy.
It is not the event that creates that hierarchy.
Thus the R2D ordering is not

singular hot point → distinctions → structure → universe.

It is
fundamental distinctions→recursive realization→boundary-defined physical geometry→hot thermal cosmological regime→later cosmological history.
The Big-Bang singularity is therefore not an unresolved candidate R2D origin.
It is the singular endpoint generated when a later continuous physical projection is extrapolated backward beyond the recursive architecture that gives that projection meaning.
The central statement is:
R2D denies the singular Big Bang as the primitive origin of reality. The zero-area, infinite-density state is generated by extrapolating a later continuum cosmological projection backward until its physical support vanishes. R2D has the opposite architecture: the largest realized boundary exists through the recursive realization of an infinitude of fundamental distinctions. The hot thermal universe is a later boundary-defined physical projection within that already-realized hierarchy, not its singular beginning.
And hence:

recursive realization occurs before the Big-Bang projection.

Here “before” is ontological and causal.
It is not a statement about extending the same FLRW time coordinate to an earlier epoch.

74. Conclusion
The Big-Bang singularity is produced by a mathematically straightforward extrapolation.
A cosmological boundary is assigned a physical area.
That area defines physical support.
Source sectors acquire area-scaling laws.
Clock calibration defines the Hubble rate.
The Friedmann projection combines those physical reads.
The same relations are then extrapolated backward toward
\[ a\to0\]
In area coordinates,
\[ A_\zeta \to  0\]
Physical support vanishes:

Vζ → 0.
Matter density diverges:
\[\epsilon_m\propto A_\zeta^{-3/2}\to\infty\]
Radiation density diverges:
\[\epsilon_r\propto A_\zeta^{-2}\to\infty\]
And the projected cosmological rate diverges.
This is the singularity of the FLRW projection.
R2D rejects the next conventional inference.
The primitive universe is not an infinite physical density inside zero geometric support.
The largest realized gear is realized recursively by an infinitude of fundamental distinctions.
Those distinctions are prior to physical volume.
They are prior to physical density.
They are prior to temperature.
They are prior to the scale factor.
They are prior to curved spacetime.
They are prior to the clock with which the singularity is assigned a finite past time.
The singular Big Bang therefore cannot be the primitive R2D state.
It reverses the causal order.
It mistakes the backward endpoint of a later physical projection for the origin of the distinctions that made that projection possible.
The hot thermal universe remains a valid physical regime.
But it is a later regime.
Its physical ruler belongs to an already-realized boundary.

Its thermal history belongs to an already-realized hierarchy.
Its backward singular extrapolation does not create that hierarchy.
The R2D architecture is instead:
fundamental distinctions→recursive realization→largest realized gear→physical cosmological projection→hot thermal history.
The singular Big-Bang architecture is:

zero physical support → all distinction and structure.

These are not two tentative interpretations of the same primitive ontology.
They are opposite ontologies.
R2D selects the former and rejects the latter.
The remaining problem is therefore no longer whether the FLRW singularity might secretly be the primitive beginning.
It is not.
The remaining constructive problem is to identify the mathematical signature by which a smooth physical cosmological projection loses the recursively realized count support required to remain continuous.
That is the point at which the old continuum description must be replaced by a boundary-defined multiplicity landscape.
The central statement is therefore:
R2D denies the singular Big Bang as the primitive origin of reality. The zero-area, infinite-density state is the endpoint of a backward extrapolation of later physical coordinates. Recursive reality has the opposite architecture: the largest realized boundary exists through the accumulated realization of an infinitude of fundamental distinctions, and physical geometry is projected only afterward. The hot thermal universe is therefore a later boundary-defined regime, not the event that creates recursive reality.
And hence:

recursive realization occurs before the Big-Bang projection.

title: Addendum 67 — Sparse Realization Occurs Before Continuum Singularity
section: Abstract
text:
Abstract

Addendum 66 established that R2D denies the singular Big Bang as the primitive origin of reality.
The largest realized boundary is recursively realized through an infinitude of fundamental distinctions.
Physical area, volume, density, temperature, curved spacetime, and cosmological clock time arise only afterward as boundary-defined physical projections.
The FLRW singularity is therefore not the origin of recursive reality.
It is the singular endpoint obtained by extrapolating a later continuum cosmological projection toward
\[ A_\zeta \to  0\]
This leaves a constructive question:

What mathematical condition marks the point at which the smooth cosmological projection ceases to resolve the recursively realized count structure from which it is constructed?

R2D already contains the required quantities.
Addendum 58 defined clock-relative cosmological progress:
\[\mathcal H_{\zeta\mid c}=\frac12\frac{d\ln A_\zeta}{dN_C^{(c)}}=\frac{d\ln a}{dN_C^{(c)}}\]
Here
\[ N_C^{(c)}\]
is the completed recurrence count of an admissible subordinate clock class.
Addendum 59 then showed, for a dominant coherent cosmological transition class χ,
\[\mathcal H_{\zeta\mid c}=\delta_{A,\chi}\rho_{\zeta\mid\zeta-1,c}\]

where
\[\delta_{A,\chi}=\frac12\ln\frac{A_{\zeta,k}}{A_{\zeta,i}}=\ln\frac{a_k}{a_i}\]
is the physical logarithmic scale step produced by one enclosing cosmological occurrence, and
\[\rho_{\zeta\mid\zeta-1,c}=\frac{N_\zeta^\chi}{N_C^{(c)}}\]
is the enclosing-occurrence/subordinate-recurrence ratio.
These quantities define a natural R2D continuum-resolution parameter:
\[ \epsilon_{\mathrm{cont}}^{(c)}\equiv\left|\frac{d\ln a}{dN_C^{(c)}}\right|=\left|\mathcal H_{\zeta\mid c}\right|. \]
For a single dominant coherent transition class,
\[ \epsilon_{\mathrm{cont}}^{(c)}=|\delta_{A,\chi}|\,\rho_{\zeta\mid\zeta-1,c}. \]
Its reciprocal is
\[ \mathcal N_{\mathrm{cont}}^{(c)}\equiv\left|\frac{dN_C^{(c)}}{d\ln a}\right|=\frac{1}{\epsilon_{\mathrm{cont}}^{(c)}}. \]
The quantity
\[\mathcal N_{\mathrm{cont}}^{(c)}\]
has a direct count interpretation.
It is the number of completed subordinate clock closures through which one order-one logarithmic change of projected cosmological scale is realized.
A smooth continuum approximation requires
\[\mathcal N_{\mathrm{cont}}^{(c)}\gg1\]
or equivalently,
\[\epsilon_{\mathrm{cont}}^{(c)}\ll1\]
Many subordinate realizations then occur within one macroscopic geometric interval.

The individual count steps are unreadable in the physical continuum coordinate.
When instead
\[\mathcal N_{\mathrm{cont}}^{(c)}=O(1)\]
the continuum interval is supported by only order-one subordinate closures.
The discrete realization path can no longer be replaced by a smooth differential trajectory without losing the count structure that generates it.
This is the R2D mathematical signature of continuum breakdown.
The resulting state is not one with few fundamental distinctions.
The largest gear remains recursively realized through an infinitude of fundamental distinctions.
The sparsity is resolution relative:

sparse realization = too few realized count updates per projected continuum interval.

It is the realized sampling of the multiplicity landscape that becomes sparse relative to the physical field coordinate.
The possible multiplicity
\[ W\]
need not become small.
Nor need primitive reality become spatially granular.
The continuum loses readability because its smooth coordinate now attempts to interpolate across distinguishable count steps rather than average over many of them.
Physical clock calibration makes the same criterion immediately visible.
Addendum 58 gave
\[ dt=T_c\,dN_C^{(c)}\]
with
\[ f_c=\frac1{T_c}=\frac{dN_C^{(c)}}{dt}\]

Therefore:
\[ H=f_c\mathcal H_{\zeta\mid c}\]
Hence:
\[ \epsilon_{\mathrm{cont}}^{(c)}=\frac{|H|}{f_c}. \]
And:
\[ \mathcal N_{\mathrm{cont}}^{(c)}=\frac{f_c}{|H|}. \]
The continuum cosmological regime therefore requires
\[|H|\ll f_c\]
The cosmological boundary must evolve slowly relative to the subordinate recurrence through which that evolution is physically resolved.
Now compare this with the fixed FLRW singular extrapolation.
For a dominant positive sector with
\[ H^2=BA_\zeta^{-s},\qquad s>0\]
one has
\[|H|=\sqrt B\,A_\zeta^{-s/2}\]
If the subordinate clock calibration remains finite over the same count domain,
\[ f_c < \infty\]
then
\[\mathcal N_{\mathrm{cont}}^{(c)}=\frac{f_c}{\sqrt B}A_\zeta^{s/2}\]
Therefore:
\[ A_\zeta\to0\quad\Longrightarrow\quad\mathcal N_{\mathrm{cont}}^{(c)}\to0\]
The fixed continuum projection necessarily passes through

\[\mathcal N_{\mathrm{cont}}^{(c)}\sim1\]
before it can reach
\[ A_\zeta = 0\]
Thus, for any finite subordinate recurrence calibration, continuum readability fails at finite projected area before the formal FLRW singularity.
There is only one way for the fixed continuum description to avoid this result.
The subordinate physical recurrence must itself increase without bound:
\[ f_c\to\infty\]
fast enough to maintain
\[|H|/f_c\ll1\]
But then the fixed clock calibration has itself failed.
The continuum has not been preserved by the same physical ruler.
It has been preserved only by moving to progressively faster subordinate recurrence structure.
That is precisely a recursive-boundary problem.
Therefore the singular extrapolation presents an R2D dichotomy:
\[|H|\to\infty\]
requires either
\[\mathcal N_{\mathrm{cont}}^{(c)}=O(1)\]
and loss of continuum readability,
or
\[ f_c\to\infty\]
and loss of the fixed physical clock calibration.
In neither case does the same smooth physical projection remain unchanged all the way to the singularity.
This supplies the mathematical bridge sought in Addendum 66.

The continuum does not become primitive reality at its singular endpoint.
Its own count-resolution parameter announces the failure of the approximation first.
The central result is:
a continuum physical trajectory is readable only while many subordinate recurrent realizations occur within each macroscopic projected change. R2D quantifies this by \(\mathcal N_{\mathrm{cont}}^{(c)}\). When this count falls from \(\mathcal N_{\mathrm{cont}}^{(c)}\gg1\) to \(\mathcal N_{\mathrm{cont}}^{(c)}=O(1)\), the smooth field trajectory ceases to be a high-count approximation and becomes a sparsely realized multiplicity path. For any finite subordinate clock calibration, the fixed FLRW singular extrapolation necessarily crosses this discrete-resolution threshold before reaching zero area.
And hence:

sparse realization occurs before continuum singularity.

77. Conclusion
The central problem left by Addendum 66 was not whether the FLRW singularity is the primitive beginning.
R2D denies that ontology.
The remaining problem was to identify the mathematical signature by which the continuum cosmological projection announces its own loss of recursive readability.
That signature already exists in the R2D rate construction.
Clock-relative cosmological progress is
\[\mathcal H_{\zeta\mid c}=\frac{d\ln a}{dN_C^{(c)}}\]
This quantity measures projected cosmological change per subordinate recurrence.
A smooth physical trajectory requires that change to be small:
\[|\mathcal H_{\zeta\mid c}|\ll1\]
Equivalently, one macroscopic logarithmic change of cosmological scale must contain many subordinate recurrent realizations:
\[\mathcal N_{\mathrm{cont}}^{(c)}=\left|\frac{dN_C^{(c)}}{d\ln a}\right|\gg1\]
This is the count architecture beneath the continuum.
For a dominant coherent occurrence class,
\[\mathcal H_{\zeta\mid c}=\delta_{A,\chi}\rho_{\zeta\mid\zeta-1,c}\]

\[ H=f_c\mathcal H_{\zeta\mid c}\]
Thus:
\[\mathcal N_{\mathrm{cont}}^{(c)}=\frac{f_c}{|H|}\]
Now apply the fixed FLRW backward scaling:

\[ H^2=BA_\zeta^{-s},\qquad s>0\]
For any finite subordinate clock calibration,
\[\mathcal N_{\mathrm{cont}}^{(c)}=\frac{f_c}{\sqrt B}A_\zeta^{s/2}\]
Therefore:
\[ A_\zeta\to0\quad\Longrightarrow\quad\mathcal N_{\mathrm{cont}}^{(c)}\to0\]
The continuum cannot remain a high-count approximation all the way to the formal singularity.
It necessarily crosses an order-one count-resolution threshold first.
If one attempts to preserve the continuum by letting
\[ f_c\to\infty\]
then the fixed physical clock calibration has instead failed and the recurrence ruler must itself be replaced.
Thus the same conclusion follows by either route.
The unchanged continuum projection does not reach the singular endpoint while retaining its original recursive meaning.
What lies beneath the failed continuum is not an infinitely compressed primitive spacetime.
It is the boundary-defined count architecture that was present before spacetime was projected at all.
Its relevant physical appearance near continuum failure is a sparsely realized multiplicity landscape:

possible multiplicity remains

while

only order-one realized count steps support each formerly smooth field interval.

This explains how conventional physical density can diverge while continuum count support becomes sparse.
The two are not opposites because they are not the same quantity.
Physical density is a downstream source/support ratio.
Sparse realization is a statement about the count resolution beneath that physical field.

The same architecture applies to cosmology and to continuum fluid singularities.
In each case:

many subordinate realizations → smooth continuum

but
loss of count separation → sparse realized multiplicity landscape → projection replacement.
The central statement is therefore:
a continuum physical law is readable only while each resolved field change is realized by many subordinate count recurrences. R2D measures that separation by the reciprocal pair \(\mathcal N_{\mathrm{cont}}^{(c)}\) and \(\epsilon_{\mathrm{cont}}^{(c)}\). Under any fixed finite clock calibration, the FLRW backward extrapolation drives \(\mathcal N_{\mathrm{cont}}^{(c)}\) from a large-count continuum regime to an order-one sparse-realization regime before zero area is reached. The singularity therefore lies beyond the count-resolution domain of the continuum projection, where the appropriate description is again a boundary-defined multiplicity landscape rather than an infinitely > compressed spacetime.
